works.title: A gene interaction network-based molecular taxonomy of dilated cardiomyopathy highlighting immune and inflammatory heterogeneity

supports: Reproducible retrospective expression-network clustering in the analyzed myocardial datasets.
Subtype-associated coexpression, enrichment and inferred immune-signature differences.
An exploratory association between EPS1 expression and the previously observed IA/IgG responder profile.
Concordant expression directions for selected genes in the specified AC16-cell stress model.
does_not_establish: Prospective diagnostic performance, prognosis or generalizability to all clinical DCM populations.
A causal mechanism for each subtype from pathway enrichment, coexpression or immune deconvolution.
A validated indication for immunoadsorption, or improved outcomes from subtype-guided treatment.
Direct immune-cell abundance measurements from ssGSEA scores.
That the cell experiment reproduces all three human subtypes or validates every inferred pathway.
A verified count of unique people across public datasets or additional independent cohorts from analysis subsets.

limitations: Public myocardial expression datasets are selected research samples; subtype prevalence and clinical transportability require further study.
The article reports that longitudinal outcome data were unavailable for prognostic evaluation.
Coexpression, enrichment and ssGSEA do not experimentally establish subtype mechanisms or immune-cell causation.
GSE19303 contributes both to subtype evaluation and to the exploratory response analysis; the response claim is not independent prospective validation.
The cell-line experiment evaluates selected EPS1-associated expression directions, with no basis to infer all subtype mechanisms or treatment effects.
The source does not provide a clinical decision threshold, calibrated individual treatment-benefit model or randomized comparison of subtype-guided care.
Supplementary-file links were verified, but the Springer supplementary spreadsheets were not retrieved successfully in this run; no claim depends on uninspected supplementary-only values.

does_not_establish: Absolute superoxide concentration in living plaques or a validated dual-wavelength PA ratio.
Clinical sensitivity, specificity, risk discrimination, prediction of plaque rupture or reduced cardiovascular events.
Human treatment efficacy of dexamethasone or clinical safety, regulatory approval or routine applicability of ReP.
A universal biological selectivity claim or complete causal demonstration of every proposed lung-to-plaque mechanism.

limitations: The evidence consists of chemical solution experiments and mouse imaging/histology. No cell-culture validation, human participants or clinical diagnostic-validation cohort is reported.

The main AS comparison has n=3 mice per group. Assay-specific measurements, repeated imaging days, tissue sections and the additional S7 sequence must not be summed into a synthetic unique animal total.

The PA calibration and in vivo result panels use intensity at 740 nm. Although introductory text uses the term ratiometric, a validated two-wavelength normalization ratio is not specified for the displayed experiments.

In vivo signals are relative aortic-region observations, not measured absolute superoxide concentrations. Probe distribution, tissue optical properties and endogenous signal are not eliminated as potential contributors by a universal biological-specificity test.
Solution selectivity applies to the reported 80 micromolar challenge panel. It does not establish complete selectivity in all tissues, across all reductants, or under every biological condition.

The figures supply calibration R-squared values but no explicit PA-calibration replicate count, limit of detection, limit of quantification, exact regression slope or calibration uncertainty. No values are reconstructed from plotted bars.
Fig. 6 heatmap percentages have no stated per-animal dispersion or statistical test. They are descriptive annotations, not independently calculated means, confidence intervals or significance claims.
Random assignment is described in the supplement; blinding, allocation concealment and an a priori sample-size calculation are not reported in the available text.

LPS/dexamethasone intervention supports experimental group contrasts; it does not independently prove every step of the proposed lung-to-systemic-oxidative-stress-to-plaque cascade, prevent rupture or demonstrate patient benefit.
Short-term body-weight and organ-histology observations have an unreported independent sample count and do not establish chronic, repeated-dose or human safety.

Supplementary affiliation/equal-contribution formatting differs from the final main-PDF author footnotes. Full author order, title, DOI and publication date agree between the main PDF, publisher and Crossref; the main version of record governs identity.

Supplementary synthetic-route temperature labeling differs from the prose description. That synthesis-temperature detail is not promoted into the evidence summary, and no unsupported protocol reconciliation is made.

works.title: Allostatic load-cardiovascular disease associations and the mediating effect of inflammatory factors: a prospective cohort study

supports: Observational population-level associations between biomarker-defined AL and incident CVD.

Validated benefits of a stress-management intervention.

limitations: Observational design does not establish causality; residual confounding remains possible.

works.title: Circadian Immunity and Vascular Inflammation in Cardiovascular Disease Chronotherapy Windows: Time for a Re-Assessment

supports: Prior evidence links circadian clock networks with immune and vascular processes, inflammatory and redox pathways.
Immune-cell number, trafficking and functional state can vary with circadian timing across experimental contexts.
Experimental circadian disruption can alter cardiovascular inflammatory phenotypes, while cardiovascular physiology and events exhibit time-of-day patterns.
Preclinical evidence provides a mechanistic rationale for chronotherapy; some cardiovascular drugs show dosing-time-dependent physiological effects.
Clinical chronotherapy remains an active and unresolved translational field.
does_not_establish: A new patient cohort, new experimental data or a newly analyzed dataset.
A systematic review, meta-analysis or pooled quantitative effect size.
One universally causal circadian pathway across all cardiovascular diseases.
Human cardiovascular treatment efficacy of REV-ERB agonists or time-targeted NLRP3 or NF-kB inhibition.
Universal superiority of bedtime antihypertensive dosing or a dosing schedule suitable for every patient.
Reduced myocardial infarction or stroke outcomes from bedtime aspirin.
Established optimal dosing for SGLT2 inhibitors, colchicine, mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists or ARNI.
A guideline-level recommendation to change cardiovascular medication timing.

limitations: This is a narrative, non-systematic evidence synthesis with no new dataset or pooled effect estimate.
Species, tissues, disease models and evidence levels are heterogeneous; causal animal or cell findings cannot automatically be generalized to human cardiovascular disease.
Constitutive and inducible clock-gene knockout models may yield different findings.
Treatment-timing evidence is uneven across cardiovascular drug classes and many proposed chronotherapy windows remain theoretical or preclinical.
Clinical antihypertensive timing evidence is conflicting, including Hygia-versus-BedMed differences.
No universal dosing recommendation is established; high-quality circadian-aware randomized clinical trials are needed.

key_findings.claim: The review places CLOCK-BMAL1, PER/CRY and REV-ERB/ROR feedback loops at the center of temporal regulation of cardiovascular immune biology.
key_findings.context: This is a synthesis of prior molecular and experimental literature rather than a new clock experiment.

evidence.label: Core clock machinery
evidence.value: BMAL1/ARNTL, CLOCK, PER1/2/3, CRY1/2, REV-ERB alpha/beta and ROR alpha/gamma are integrated with redox and epigenetic regulation.

key_findings.source_locator: Sections 2.1-2.4; Figures 1-2; Tables 1-2.

key_findings.claim: Circadian timing is synthesized as a regulator of PRR, NF-kB and NLRP3 inflammatory signaling and of cytokine, chemokine and adhesion-molecule rhythms.
key_findings.context: These mechanisms derive from heterogeneous experimental systems and should not be represented as one fully demonstrated causal human pathway.

evidence.label: Inflammatory networks
evidence.value: The review discusses IL-1beta, IL-6, IL-18, TNF-alpha, CCL2, CXCL12, ICAM1, VCAM1 and related inflammatory networks.

key_findings.source_locator: Sections 3-4; Figure 3; Table 3.

key_findings.claim: The review describes circadian variation in immune-cell number, trafficking and function across neutrophils, monocytes/macrophages, lymphocytes and dendritic cells.
key_findings.context: Timing, phase and mechanisms vary by species, tissue and experimental model.

evidence.label: Trafficking mechanisms
evidence.value: BMAL1, chemokine axes, sympathetic signaling and cell-intrinsic clocks are synthesized as contributors to rhythmic immune trafficking and function.

key_findings.source_locator: Section 5; Figures 4-5.

key_findings.claim: Circadian disruption is reviewed in relation to atherosclerosis, stroke, ischemic heart disease/myocardial infarction and heart failure through overlapping inflammatory, endothelial, metabolic and oxidative-stress mechanisms.
key_findings.context: Evidence strength and causality differ materially across disease, mechanism and model.

evidence.label: Disease domains
evidence.value: The synthesis compares atherosclerosis, stroke, ischemic heart disease, myocardial infarction and heart failure rather than reporting one new cross-disease experiment.

key_findings.source_locator: Sections 6.1-6.4; Figures 6-8.

key_findings.claim: Preclinical studies provide a mechanistic rationale for time-dependent intervention targeting clock and inflammatory pathways.
key_findings.context: This evidence is predominantly preclinical and must not be converted into human treatment-efficacy claims.

evidence.label: Preclinical strategies
evidence.value: The review discusses REV-ERB agonists, NLRP3 inhibitors, NF-kB pathway modulation, CCR2/CCL2 and CXCL12/CXCR4 strategies.

key_findings.source_locator: Section 7.1; Table 4.

key_findings.claim: Clinical chronotherapy evidence is heterogeneous and does not define a universal optimal dosing time for most cardiovascular drugs.
key_findings.context: Physiological timing effects and mechanistic rationale are not equivalent to proven reductions in clinical outcomes.

evidence.label: Drug classes and timing
evidence.value: The review discusses aspirin, beta-blockers, melatonin, tPA, SGLT2 inhibitors, colchicine, ACEIs/ARBs, MRAs, ARNI and antihypertensive timing.

evidence.label: Conflicting trials
evidence.value: Hygia and related studies reported bedtime-dosing benefits, whereas BedMed did not reproduce a cardiovascular-event benefit.

key_findings.source_locator: Section 7.2; Table 5.

key_findings.claim: The review identifies unresolved methodological and translational gaps that limit precision chronotherapy.
key_findings.context: These gaps are part of the authors' discussion, not newly experimentally tested findings.

evidence.label: Research gaps
evidence.value: Constitutive-versus-inducible knockout-model differences, immune-cell-subpopulation heterogeneity, insufficient spatiotemporal resolution of vascular-immune interactions and the need for high-quality circadian-aware clinical trials are highlighted.

key_findings.source_locator: Sections 8.1-8.4.

key_findings.claim: Chronotherapy claims in this review require explicit separation of mechanistic rhythmicity, preclinical time-of-day efficacy, human surrogate effects and hard cardiovascular outcomes.
key_findings.context: These evidence levels are not interchangeable. Human clinical timing evidence remains incomplete or conflicting for many cardiovascular therapies.

evidence.label: Human timing evidence
evidence.value: Bedtime aspirin can alter morning platelet reactivity, but cardiovascular event reduction has not been established by a large randomized trial; SGLT2-inhibitor and colchicine timing remain insufficiently tested.

evidence.label: Outcome-level uncertainty
evidence.value: Antihypertensive bedtime-dosing studies have reported conflicting cardiovascular outcome results, including the Hygia and BedMed trials.

key_findings.source_locator: Section 7.2; Table 5; Sections 8.1-8.4.

works.title: Combining Insulin Resistance and Renal Function to Predict Cardiovascular Events: A Multicenter Cohort Study
review_topics: Combined metabolic and renal risk assessment

supports: Prospective observational associations between the baseline ratio and incident CVD/CHD in the analyzed UK Biobank population.
Independent association replication for MACE in a small, complete-case hospital cohort.
Exploratory network analysis and further research into integrated cardiometabolic–renal markers.
does_not_establish: A causal effect of the ratio on cardiovascular disease or a confirmed biological mechanism.
A statistically significant highest-versus-lowest-quartile stroke association in fully adjusted Model 3.
An independently calibrated individual-risk calculator, improved C-statistic/NRI/IDI, or superiority to established risk scores.
A universal clinical cut-off, treatment efficacy, or benefit from targeting the ratio.
That exposure-quartile network differences demonstrate within-person disease transitions.

limitations: The observational design cannot establish causation and residual confounding remains possible.
UK Biobank selection and demographic composition limit generalizability.
The external cohort was from one clinical center; only a complete-case subset entered the fully adjusted analysis, limiting precision and representativeness.
The source reports different results for continuous, quartile, and spline contrasts; these should not be collapsed into one uniform association.
Incremental discrimination, calibration, reclassification, and clinical decision benefit beyond established risk scores were not established.
Exploratory network comparisons between exposure quartiles cannot demonstrate longitudinal within-person phase transitions.

works.title: PAPPA2 c.392G>C Heterozygous Mutation Associates Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma in a Chinese Family
review_topics: PAPPA2 and IGFBP5 in ocular fibrosis-associated responses
Comparison of variant-expression assays and gene-deficiency models

supports: Lower PAPPA2 protein abundance with mutant expression in the reported 293T assay.
Attenuation of IGFBP5-associated molecular responses by PAPPA2 cotreatment in the specified primary-cell conditions.
Elevated pressure and increased trabecular collagen-associated staining in the specified Pappa2-deficient mouse comparison.
does_not_establish: Independently reconciled family-wide counts, complete segregation, population allele frequency, penetrance or clinical pathogenicity of PAPPA2 c.392G>C.
A directly measured change in PAPPA2 protein half-life from endpoint protein and mRNA assays alone.
Equivalence of Pappa2 deficiency to the exact human p.Gly131Ala variant.
Human diagnostic performance, glaucoma prevention, treatment efficacy or safety.

limitations: Results 3.1-3.2 describe a family association, but the Figure 1a caption does not fully specify which depicted relatives contribute to the reported counts, and Figure 2a-b provides representative Sanger traces rather than an individual-level genotype table. The page therefore does not validate family-wide counts or complete segregation; it does not substitute an alternative count inferred from symbols.
The mutant expression assay measured endpoint protein abundance and mRNA. It did not directly measure protein half-life, secretion rate, or clinical variant penetrance.
The primary-cell experiments used two donor-derived lines. Three experimental repeats and multiple cells imaged within each experiment do not increase the number of independent human donors.

The mouse study used five animals per genotype. Deficiency of Pappa2 is not equivalent to an exact missense-variant knock-in, and pressure and collagen-associated staining do not establish the full human glaucoma phenotype.
No human therapeutic intervention, clinical diagnostic validation, or patient outcome benefit is established by the experimental findings summarized here.

works.title: System biology analysis reveals circadian rhythm disorder associated with development and progression in colorectal cancer

supports: The article defines a 906-gene colon circadian reference and derives CRC-associated circadian co-expression structure from a 94,683-cell single-cell dataset.
ClockProCRC uses expression-matched random-background correction and varies in expected directions across multiple experimentally or behaviorally perturbed circadian datasets.
Higher ClockProCRC values are associated with CRC progression-related states and poorer overall survival in the analyzed retrospective/public cohorts.
ClockProCRC-defined states are associated with distinct CRC single-cell composition and intercellular-communication patterns.
SYNE1 is prioritized by gene-regulatory-network analysis and shows circadian perturbation-associated expression/rhythmicity changes across independent datasets.
SYNE1 knockdown in HCT116 and SW480 cells reduces migration, invasion and colony formation and shifts E-cadherin, ZO-1 and N-cadherin expression.
CLOCK knockdown and melatonin rescue conditions alter ClockProCRC and SYNE1 rhythmicity in CRC-cell experiments.
does_not_establish: That ClockProCRC has been prospectively validated in a multicenter clinical cohort.
That ClockProCRC is a clinically approved diagnostic, prognostic, screening or treatment-selection test.
That the cohort-specific median or single-cell 75th-percentile grouping rules define a universal clinical cutoff.
That higher ClockProCRC causally drives CRC progression in humans; most clinical and tumor-microenvironment evidence is observational or retrospective.
That ClockProCRC adds incremental clinical utility over established CRC staging, molecular markers or treatment-response assessment.
That SYNE1 is a validated therapeutic target in patients with CRC.
That SYNE1 inhibition improves tumor control, metastasis or survival in vivo; the study reports cell-line perturbation but no SYNE1-directed animal efficacy experiment.
That melatonin treatment is effective for CRC patients; melatonin was used as a molecular rescue condition in cell experiments.
That AUC=0.915 represents CRC diagnosis or patient-level prediction; it refers to discrimination of CLOCK-knockdown experimental conditions by SYNE1 expression.
That single-cell ligand-receptor and pathway analyses prove causal tumor-microenvironment remodeling.

limitations: Most human clinical evidence derives from retrospective/public transcriptomic datasets rather than a prospectively enrolled multicenter clinical validation cohort.
The study integrates heterogeneous evidence units across human, mouse and non-human-primate datasets; sample, tissue, cohort and cell counts are not interchangeable.
ClockProCRC grouping uses data-context-specific thresholds (75th percentile for single-cell analyses and commonly the cohort median for bulk cohorts), not a universal clinical cutoff.

The manuscript distinguishes the 906-gene colon circadian reference from the 559-gene four-module CTD signature. The ClockProCRC scoring Methods refers to circadian rhythm disorder genes (CRGs), so this evidence page does not infer that the 559 CTD genes are identical to the final score-input gene set.

The Results text contains the accession GSE200977, whereas the Methods and Figure 4 legend identify the CRC single-cell cohort as GSE200997; the evidence page uses GSE200997 and records the Results-text accession as a manuscript typo.

The manuscript contains several wording/locator inconsistencies, including knockdown described once as knockout, Transwell language that conflates proliferation with migration/invasion, and a scratch-assay timing inconsistency; the evidence page follows the experimental Methods and figure legends.

The public ClockProCRC GitHub repository is an associated code resource but does not exactly mirror the accepted manuscript: the README reports an earlier 32-cohort/3,075-sample configuration, the current scoring script defaults to 50 bins rather than the manuscript's 100 bins, and DiffCircadian.R contains a placeholder scoring function.
SYNE1 functional evidence is in vitro; no SYNE1-directed animal efficacy experiment or human therapeutic study is reported.
The publisher currently labels the article as an early peer-reviewed accepted version that may undergo further editing before the final Version of Record.

works.title: The cholesterol, high-density lipoprotein, and glucose index and its derivatives related to obesity and inflammation as novel metabolic markers for predicting new-onset cardiovascular-liver-metabolic multimorbidity: A prospective cohort study

Hypothesis generation and independent validation of accessible metabolic-marker combinations.
does_not_establish: A causal effect of CHG, obesity, or inflammation on multimorbidity.
Imaging- or biopsy-confirmed MASLD in every participant.
Hazard ratios, exact onset timing, or a time-to-event prediction model.
Independent internal or external validation, clinical net benefit, treatment efficacy, or a validated clinical cut-off.

limitations: Residual confounding and observational design prevent causal inference.

Generalizability beyond Chinese adults aged at least 45 years requires independent evaluation.

works.title: Vascular smooth muscle cell-derived KIF13B inhibits proinflammatory responses to protect against atherosclerosis

supports: Association between lower KIF13B and more advanced or unstable human atherosclerotic plaque features across local tissue and independent public datasets.
A causal contribution of VSMC Kif13b loss to measured atherosclerotic plaque phenotypes in the tested male mouse models.
Cell-autonomous effects of KIF13B gain and loss on matrix, inflammatory and contractile programs in primary HASMCs.
Functional placement of KLF4 downstream of KIF13B in HASMC perturbation and rescue experiments.
Evidence consistent with KCTD10-mediated KLF4 ubiquitination and proteasomal turnover downstream of KIF13B.
Preclinical cellular and mouse rescue after Kenpaullone exposure under the tested conditions.
does_not_establish: That low KIF13B expression or KIF13B methylation causes plaque instability in humans.
That KIF13B, KCTD10, KLF4 or Kenpaullone has proven therapeutic efficacy or safety in patients with atherosclerosis.
That Kenpaullone is selective for KLF4 or that all Kenpaullone effects in this study are mediated specifically through KLF4.
A universal lipid-independent KIF13B mechanism in humans; the reported absence of TC/TG differences applies to the tested mouse comparison.
Independent replication of the study-generated single-cell comparison, because five mice were pooled into one library per genotype.
One definitive single-cell diet duration or one unambiguous cluster assignment for every Figure 5-7 subpanel where the article text and captions disagree.
The molecular mechanism by which KIF13B regulates KCTD10 abundance.
Generalization of the causal or pharmacologic mouse findings to females, because only male mice were used.

limitations: The local human cohort contained six carotid endarterectomy patients with paired within-plaque regions; human observations are associative and small-sample.
The local advanced-versus-adjacent classification was based on anatomical location and macroscopic surgical appearance rather than molecular or histopathological criteria.
Stable/unstable public datasets and local advanced/adjacent paired regions use different plaque definitions and should not be treated as interchangeable cohorts.
Human methylation observations are associative and do not establish that KIF13B hypermethylation causes KIF13B downregulation or plaque instability.
The PXD062283 repository contains 87 plaques overall, whereas the JCI stable/unstable comparison uses a subset of 19 and 38; repository size and analytical subset must not be conflated.
Five mice were pooled into one single-cell library per genotype, limiting independent biological replication at the single-cell library level.
Figure 5/Results report a 20-week Western-diet single-cell experiment, whereas downstream Figure 6/7 captions reference 12 weeks; this discrepancy is unresolved.
Results describe inflammatory genes in VSMC-Fib4 while the Figure 5K caption labels the panel VSMC-Fib1; the evidence page therefore avoids treating that subpanel label as unambiguous.
Only male mice were used, and sex was not analyzed as a biological variable.
Tagln-Cre targets smooth-muscle compartments beyond plaque VSMCs; reported intestine/bladder measurements do not establish general systemic safety of pathway targeting.
The study establishes KCTD10-dependent KLF4 ubiquitination/rescue evidence but does not identify the mechanism by which KIF13B regulates KCTD10 abundance.
Kenpaullone is pharmacologically nonselective; its rescue does not prove KLF4-selective target engagement or exclude contributions from other kinase targets.
Kenpaullone was evaluated only in cells and mice. No human atherosclerosis efficacy, dosing, pharmacokinetic or safety trial was performed.

key_findings.claim: Lower KIF13B was associated with more advanced or unstable human atherosclerotic plaque states, with prominent differences in VSMCs.
key_findings.context: These human tissue and public-dataset observations are associative and do not establish that changing KIF13B alters plaque outcomes in patients.

evidence.label: Local carotid plaques
evidence.value: Six CEA patients contributed paired advanced and adjacent regions; Figure 1 reports lower KIF13B in advanced regions, with scRNA analysis n=4 per condition and protein/histologic analyses n=6 per condition.

evidence.label: GSE120521
evidence.value: KIF13B mRNA was lower in unstable than stable regions from four paired carotid plaques: n=4 stable and n=4 unstable.

evidence.label: PXD062283
evidence.value: KIF13B protein was lower in the JCI stable n=19 versus unstable n=38 plaque comparison.

evidence.label: Plaque matrix relationship
evidence.value: Human plaque analysis showed lower VSMC KIF13B and lower collagen in advanced regions, with a positive association between VSMC KIF13B signal and collagen content.

evidence.label: Epigenetic evidence
evidence.value: Supplementary public-dataset reanalysis associated higher KIF13B methylation with atherosclerotic versus control tissue and symptomatic versus asymptomatic plaque; this does not establish methylation as the cause of lower KIF13B.

key_findings.source_locator: Results: Decreased expression of KIF13B in VSMCs is linked to the progression of atherosclerosis in humans; Figure 1; Supplemental Figure 1; Methods: Human studies.

key_findings.claim: VSMC-specific Kif13b deletion worsened experimental atherosclerotic lesion and plaque-stability phenotypes in male AAV8-PCSK9 mice without detected differences in plasma total cholesterol or triglycerides in the tested model.
key_findings.context: This supports a causal VSMC contribution in this mouse model; it does not establish a universally lipid-independent mechanism in humans.

evidence.label: Model
evidence.value: Male Kif13b floxed and VSMC-specific Kif13b-KO mice received AAV8-PCSK9-D377Y and Western diet for 20 weeks; major comparisons n=8 per group.

evidence.label: Plaque phenotype
evidence.value: Kif13b loss increased aortic and aortic-root lesion burden, necrotic-core area, CD68-positive macrophage accumulation and TUNEL-positive cells, while reducing collagen and plaque-stability features.

evidence.label: Plasma lipids
evidence.value: No detected genotype difference in plasma total cholesterol or triglycerides was reported in the primary Western-diet comparison.

evidence.label: Vascular function
evidence.value: Phenylephrine-induced aortic-ring contraction was impaired with VSMC Kif13b loss; n=4 per group.

key_findings.source_locator: Results: Depletion of Kif13b in VSMCs exacerbates atherosclerosis in mice; Figure 2.

key_findings.claim: The pooled mouse aortic single-cell comparison linked KIF13B loss to a shift from matrix/collagen-associated VSMC-derived states toward inflammatory programs.
key_findings.context: Five mice were pooled into one library per genotype, limiting independent library-level replication. Figure captions also contain unresolved duration and cluster-label inconsistencies, so this page reports the robust program-level conclusion rather than over-resolving ambiguous subpanel labels.

evidence.label: Single-cell design
evidence.value: Ldlr-deficient and Ldlr-deficient Kif13b-deficient aortas used five pooled mice to create one single-cell sample per genotype.

evidence.label: Cell-state programs
evidence.value: KIF13B loss was associated with reduced extracellular-matrix/collagen programs and increased apoptosis/inflammatory programs, with fewer matrix-associated VSMC-Fib states and more inflammatory VSMC-Fib states.

evidence.label: Duration discrepancy
evidence.value: Figure 5 and Results describe 20 weeks of Western diet; Figure 6 SCENIC and Figure 7 integrative captions reference 12 weeks. The discrepancy is retained rather than resolved.

evidence.label: Cluster-label discrepancy
evidence.value: Results assign the inflammatory Ccl2/Il1b/Il6/Il18/Trap1 signal to VSMC-Fib4, while Figure 5K caption labels the panel VSMC-Fib1; no unqualified cluster-specific gene claim is made here.

key_findings.source_locator: Results: Inhibiting KIF13B promotes proinflammatory fibroblast-like VSMC transition; Figures 5-7.

key_findings.claim: KIF13B gain- and loss-of-function directly altered matrix, inflammatory and contractile phenotypes in primary human aortic smooth muscle cells under oxLDL.
key_findings.context: These are cell-autonomous in vitro perturbation experiments and do not demonstrate a patient treatment effect.

evidence.label: KIF13B knockdown
evidence.value: Knockdown reduced TAGLN, collagen secretion and collagen-gel contraction while increasing fibroblast/inflammatory features; Western/ELISA assays generally n=3 and gel contraction n=5.

evidence.label: KIF13B overexpression
evidence.value: Overexpression produced reciprocal matrix/contractile effects; Western/ELISA assays generally n=3 and gel contraction n=6.

key_findings.source_locator: Results: Inhibiting KIF13B promotes proinflammatory fibroblast-like VSMC transition; Figure 5L-Q and Supplemental Figure 3.

key_findings.claim: KLF4 functionally mediated KIF13B-loss-associated VSMC reprogramming in primary HASMC experiments.
key_findings.context: The rescue establishes a downstream functional relationship in this experimental system, not a causal human clinical mechanism.

evidence.label: KLF4 response
evidence.value: KIF13B knockdown increased KLF4 protein, whereas KIF13B overexpression decreased it; Western blot n=3 and selected immunofluorescence n=10.

evidence.label: Genetic rescue
evidence.value: Concomitant KLF4 knockdown rescued KIF13B-loss-associated reductions in collagen/matrix markers and increases in inflammatory factors; Western, qPCR and ELISA assays n=3.

key_findings.source_locator: Results: KLF4 mediates KIF13B-dependent proinflammatory VSMC reprogramming; Figure 6.

key_findings.claim: Proteostasis and rescue experiments support KCTD10-dependent KLF4 ubiquitination and proteasomal turnover downstream of KIF13B.
key_findings.context: Molecular docking was predictive, while KCTD10-KLF4 association, ubiquitination and rescue were experimentally evaluated. The upstream mechanism by which KIF13B maintains KCTD10 abundance remains unresolved.

evidence.label: KLF4 turnover
evidence.value: CHX chase, MG132 and KLF4 ubiquitination assays showed that KIF13B knockdown stabilized KLF4 by attenuating proteasomal degradation; n=3 independent biological replicates.

evidence.label: KCTD10 identification
evidence.value: Integrated mouse VSMC and human unstable/stable plaque transcriptomics nominated KCTD10 and SKP1; KIF13B perturbation altered KCTD10 rather than SKP1 in HASMC protein assays.

evidence.label: KCTD10-KLF4 mechanism
evidence.value: Docking predicted interaction; co-IP supported KCTD10-KLF4 association, KCTD10 overexpression increased KLF4 ubiquitination and reduced KLF4 protein.

evidence.label: KCTD10 rescue
evidence.value: KCTD10 overexpression reversed KIF13B-knockdown-associated KLF4 stabilization and rescued collagen/inflammatory phenotypes.

key_findings.source_locator: Results: KIF13B facilitates KCTD10-mediated ubiquitination and degradation of KLF4; Figures 7-8 and Supplemental Figure 4.

key_findings.claim: Kenpaullone reduced KLF4 promoter activity/expression and produced preclinical rescue of KIF13B-loss-associated cellular and mouse plaque phenotypes.
key_findings.context: Kenpaullone is not established as a KLF4-selective drug. Authoritative pharmacology sources describe it as an ATP-competitive CDK/GSK3β inhibitor. The rescue therefore supports preclinical pathway modulation but does not prove KLF4-selective pharmacology or human treatment efficacy.

evidence.label: Cell intervention
evidence.value: Kenpaullone at 10 µM reduced KLF4 and rescued collagen/inflammatory phenotypes after KIF13B knockdown in HASMCs; n=3 biological replicates for key Western/ELISA assays.

evidence.label: Mouse intervention
evidence.value: Male PCSK9 mice received oral Kenpaullone 1 mg/kg/day for the final 12 weeks of a 20-week Western-diet protocol; n=6 per group.

evidence.label: Mouse outcomes
evidence.value: Kenpaullone reduced measured inflammatory cytokines, lesion burden, necrotic-core area, CD68-positive macrophages and TUNEL-positive cells and increased collagen.

evidence.label: Measured safety-related endpoints
evidence.value: No detected changes were reported in measured body weight, plasma TC/TG or ALT/AST endpoints; these measurements do not establish general or human safety.

key_findings.source_locator: Results: Pharmacological inhibition of KLF4 with Kenpaullone alleviates atherosclerosis in mice; Figure 9 and Supplemental Figures 5-7.

study_profile.study_design: Mechanistic translational preclinical study integrating associative human plaque observations and public multi-omic datasets with causal mouse genetics, pooled single-cell RNA sequencing, primary HASMC perturbation, biochemical rescue and preclinical pharmacologic intervention.
study_profile.evidence_type: Associative human tissue and multi-omic evidence; causal mouse genetics; primary human VSMC perturbation; biochemical mechanism and rescue; preclinical pharmacologic rescue.
study_profile.population: Paired carotid endarterectomy plaque regions from 6 patients; independent public human plaque datasets; male mouse atherosclerosis models; primary human aortic smooth muscle cells. No treated human atherosclerosis cohort.
study_profile.primary_endpoint: Experimental atherosclerotic lesion burden, plaque-stability features and VSMC phenotypic remodeling across genetic models.
study_profile.secondary_endpoint: Collagen and extracellular-matrix programs, inflammatory cytokines, VSMC contractile function, KLF4 protein regulation, KCTD10-dependent ubiquitination and preclinical pharmacologic rescue.
data_modalities: Paired human carotid plaque histology and protein analysis
Human plaque single-cell and spatial transcriptomic analysis
Mouse plaque histology and plasma phenotyping
Primary HASMC gain- and loss-of-function assays
Protein stability, ubiquitination and co-immunoprecipitation assays

scale_metrics.label: Local paired carotid CEA cohort
scale_metrics.value: 6 patients. Each plaque supplied an advanced/culprit region and an adjacent upstream region from the same patient. Figure 1 reports scRNA analysis n=4 regions per condition and Western/histologic analyses n=6 regions per condition; these are paired regions, not 10 or 12 independent participants.

scale_metrics.label: GSE120521
scale_metrics.value: 4 carotid endarterectomy patients, each contributing paired stable and unstable plaque regions: 4 stable and 4 unstable RNA-seq samples.

scale_metrics.label: PXD062283
scale_metrics.value: The ProteomeXchange repository contains 87 human carotid plaques overall; the JCI Figure 1 comparison uses stable n=19 and unstable n=38. Do not substitute the repository total for the study subset.

scale_metrics.value: Three independent public methylation datasets were reanalyzed in the Supplement. Dataset-specific denominators must remain separate and must not be summed into a synthetic human cohort.

scale_metrics.label: VSMC-specific PCSK9 mouse model
scale_metrics.value: 8-week-old male Kif13b floxed and Tagln-Cre Kif13b VSMC-KO mice received AAV8-PCSK9-D377Y and Western diet for 20 weeks; primary pathology, lipid and cytokine comparisons n=8 per group; aortic-ring assays n=4 per group.

scale_metrics.label: Mouse single-cell experiment
scale_metrics.value: Ldlr-deficient versus Ldlr-deficient Kif13b-deficient mice; five mice were pooled into one aortic single-cell library per genotype. Figure 5/Results report 20-week Western diet, while downstream Figure 6/7 captions reference 12-week Western diet.

scale_metrics.label: Primary HASMC perturbation
scale_metrics.value: KIF13B knockdown and overexpression under oxLDL were assessed with Western blot/ELISA biological replicates generally n=3; collagen-gel contraction used n=5 for knockdown and n=6 for overexpression.

scale_metrics.label: KLF4 and KCTD10 rescue
scale_metrics.value: KLF4 dual-knockdown and KCTD10-overexpression biochemical and phenotypic rescue assays generally used n=3 independent biological replicates; selected immunofluorescence assays used n=10.

scale_metrics.label: Kenpaullone intervention
scale_metrics.value: HASMC experiments used 10 µM Kenpaullone. Male PCSK9 mice received 1 mg/kg/day orally during the final 12 weeks of a 20-week Western-diet protocol; n=6 per group.

study_profile.counting_note: Human participants, paired plaque regions, public dataset samples, mice, pooled single-cell libraries and independent cell-culture replicates are different denominators and must not be summed. External human datasets provide cross-source corroboration, not prospective clinical validation. Five mice pooled into one library per genotype are not five independent single-cell libraries. Preserve the paper's figure-specific 20-week versus 12-week single-cell duration descriptions rather than harmonizing them.

works.title: A Multimodal artificial intelligence framework for mechanistic discovery and digital twin construction in cardiovascular medicine
review_topics: Multimodal AI for cardiovascular mechanism research
Digital modeling and prospective evaluation requirements

supports: Cite for framing a cardiovascular AI research agenda around mechanistic questions and individualized digital modeling, not for product validation.
Cite for the methodological rationale of cross-modal hypothesis generation; causal claims require suitable primary experimental evidence.
Cite as design background for physiological modeling and scenario simulation, not as evidence that a drug, surgery or commercial digital twin improves outcomes.
Cite when discussing evaluation, data stewardship and implementation requirements; prospective benefit remains a question for future empirical assessment.
does_not_establish: A newly developed, validated therapeutic digital twin or completed prospective clinical validation in this Correspondence.
Causation established by combining imaging and molecular data alone.

works.title: Mapping heterogeneous molecular subtypes of circadian misalignment underlying lung adenocarcinoma risk
review_topics: Retrospective subtype associations and treatment-response hypotheses

supports: Retrospective LUAD expression clustering and cross-cohort NTP assessment under the reported confidence filtering.
Reported outcome, pathway, genomic and inferred immune associations for expression-defined clusters.
Computational treatment hypotheses and article-reported within-TCGA signature comparisons, with source gaps retained.
does_not_establish: A prospective subtype-guided clinical trial, treatment benefit or clinical decision rule.
Direct measurement of patient circadian phase, sleep behavior or causal circadian mechanisms.
Immunotherapy response rates, benefit probabilities or chemotherapy/corticosteroid recommendations for the subtypes.
A deduplicated unique-patient total spanning LUAD and immunotherapy datasets.
Externally validated best-signature performance, calibration, decision benefit or resolved Chen EG model attribution.
Resolved author order, dates or pagination across the conflicting official bibliographic records.

limitations: Retrospective and largely computational evidence; no prospective subtype-guided treatment trial or direct patient circadian-physiology experiment is reported.
The seven LUAD input counts sum arithmetically to 2090. Participant-level disjointness is not established, and the separately reported 79 immunotherapy records are not added to claim a unique total.
NTP confidence filtering and incomplete clinical information alter analysis denominators. The input cohort counts are not every downstream survival, genomic or prediction denominator.
Validation Results say five external cohorts while naming six GEO accessions. Six named cohorts are described; accession differences alone do not prove patient disjointness.
The adopted PDF swaps Figure 2/3 captions relative to visual content: PDF p. 6 / print p. 19 is enrichment; PDF p. 8 / print p. 21 is proportions/survival. Locators identify actual page and content.
Template-feature heatmap labels conflict with referenced cohort names: one says GSE64865 and another says GSE42127 where its caption says GSE41271. Their identity is not repaired by guess.

The 79 immunotherapy reference records lack a verified cohort split, adequately identified second source, tumor-histology breakdown and overlap crosswalk. Data availability cites references 60/61 absent from the supplied list ending at 52.
TIS, checkpoint expression and SubMap are indirect predictions or similarity analyses, not actual response rates, benefit probabilities or a recommendation to give immunotherapy to C3 patients.
Drug text/axis IC50 versus estimated-AUC and prednisone versus prednisolone discrepancies are retained. Predicted sensitivity does not establish clinical chemotherapy or corticosteroid benefit.

The 151-signature comparison ranks recalculated candidates within TCGA. The reported best C-index values do not establish external validation, calibration, decision benefit or resolved Chen EG model attribution.

Supplementary legends mention S3/S4 silhouette and survival analyses, but the supplied official ZIP contains only S1/S2 images. Their unavailable adjusted hazard ratios, confidence intervals and independent prognostic claims are not supplied.
Table S1 contains 2091 listed entries including apparent spreadsheet date-conversion tokens. They are not corrected or used to assert an independently reproduced clean gene signature.

works.title: Modeling Diabetic Cardiomyopathy Using Human Cardiac Organoids: Effects of High Glucose and Lipid Conditions

supports: The described generation and marker characterization of hiPSC-derived cardiac organoids.
The reported viability-screen pattern and selected apoptosis, inflammatory and fibrosis-associated group observations in the acquired pre-proof.
A descriptive metformin-labeled group comparison, with the absent dose and unresolved biological replicate count explicitly disclosed.
does_not_establish: Clinical diagnostic accuracy, patient benefit, prevention of diabetic heart disease or a glucose target for patients.
A validated metformin dose, treatment regimen, safety profile or clinical effect size.
Independent biological replication across a known number of donors or a complete reproduction protocol.
A reconciled TNNT2/MYH6 expression direction, verified JC-1 ratio orientation, calibrated contractile force or measured mitochondrial respiratory capacity.
Equivalence of every detail in the pre-proof and definitive final full text, or independent verification of the two unavailable supplementary files.

limitations: The reviewed source is a 37-page publisher-branded Journal Pre-proof obtained through the author-authorized ResearchGate private-file channel. It is not the definitive version of record. DOI, title and all 14 authors agree with the current Crossref record, publisher landing page and PubMed record, but full final-text equivalence has not been verified.

The study is an in vitro experiment using human-derived cells, not a human clinical cohort or an animal experiment. hiPSC line identifiers, independent donor number and the biological versus technical replicate unit are not clearly reported; caption n=3/n=6 values must not be converted into a unique human n.

Methods 2.14 describes experiments conducted at least three times, mean +/- SD and one-way ANOVA. A post-hoc procedure, multiplicity strategy, randomization, blinded outcome assessment and a prospective sample-size calculation are not specified in the acquired source.

TNNT2 and MYH6 are not included as accepted directional findings: Results 3.4 and 3.7 describe marker increases too broadly, whereas Figs. 3D/H and 7 display lower TNNT2/MYH6 in relevant treatment groups than control. No text or figure direction is silently chosen as a correction.

JC-1 findings are excluded from directional or quantitative conclusions: Methods 2.11 specifies a red/green ratio, while Fig. 6B labels green/red. Reported fluorescence-channel wavelengths also require clarification. No mitochondrial respiration or ATP measurement was reported; membrane-potential fluorescence cannot establish respiratory capacity.

The metformin concentration is absent from the inspected methods, results and legends. The labeled-group observations are described without an inferred regimen, dose-response claim, percentage rescue or extrapolation to patient efficacy.

The culture methods print 10 mM for Y-27632, CHIR99021 and IWR-1. These values are not silently changed to micromolar concentrations and are not offered as an independently verified reproduction protocol.

The glucose-alone figure displays a 5 mM baseline but no glucose-free group; its control terminology differs from the text. No exact clinical or in vitro toxicity threshold is certified. No explicit osmotic-control experiment is reported.

Figure 3A measures diameter excursion in micrometers, despite use of the word force in the text. It is not a calibrated mechanical-force measurement, and no claim of validated cardiac pumping performance is made.

Supplementary files 1 and 2 are cited but were not present in the acquired PDF or retrieved from an accessible official channel. Their dynamic contraction and high-dose morphology material is not treated as viewed or independently verified.

works.title: The macrophage-derived motor protein KIF13B enhances MERTK-mediated efferocytosis and prevents atherosclerosis in mice

supports: Association between lower KIF13B and advanced human arterial or carotid-plaque tissue, and progression in mouse plaque observations.
Causal worsening of mouse plaque phenotypes after global, myeloid or hematopoietic Kif13b perturbation within their respective experimental models.

A myeloid or hematopoietic contribution without corresponding plasma-lipid differences in conditional and transplantation models, separate from the lipid increase in global Ldlr-deficient knockout mice.
Reduced MERTK protein and efferocytosis after Kif13b loss and improvement of BMDM efferocytosis following MERTK restoration.
Evidence consistent with post-translational ITCH/CBL/MERTK regulation and article-reported NX-1607 rescue in macrophages and mice.
does_not_establish: Human KIF13B causality, prediction of clinical outcomes or human atherosclerosis treatment efficacy.
That the global Ldlr-deficient knockout plaque phenotype is lipid independent.
Macrophage-exclusive effects of Lyz2-Cre deletion or bone-marrow transplantation, or five independent single-cell libraries from five pooled mice.
One definitive diet duration for the study-generated pooled aortic single-cell comparison, because Results and Figure 3E disagree.
That MERTK restoration is an effective in vivo or human therapy, or that every proposed ITCH-to-CBL ubiquitination and degradation step has been directly resolved.

That NX-1607 reverses 20 weeks of established disease, has proven human atherosclerosis benefit, or unequivocally validates endogenous CBL rather than the distinct CBLB target described by external sources.

limitations: Human arterial-wall and carotid-plaque results are associative tissue observations with small carotid groups, not causal human intervention evidence.
The global Kif13b-deficient Ldlr model had higher circulating cholesterol and triglycerides, limiting attribution of its plaque phenotype solely to local plaque biology.
Lyz2-Cre targets myeloid lineages and donor-marrow transplantation changes hematopoietic compartments; neither isolates macrophages exclusively.
Study-generated single-cell data pooled five mice to one library per genotype, limiting independent biological replication at the library level.
The Results and Figure 3E give discordant 20-week Western-diet and 12-week high-fat-diet descriptions for the pooled aortic single-cell experiment.
GSE155513 Figure 3 time points use one single-cell library each; sample and library counts must not be conflated.
MERTK restoration rescue was demonstrated in Kif13b-deficient BMDMs, not as an in vivo MERTK treatment.
The exact ITCH-mediated CBL ubiquitination/degradation step in the proposed network remains incompletely demonstrated; MERTK regulation is not fully assigned to one mechanism.
The article's CBL-inhibitor description of NX-1607 conflicts with external CBL-B/CBLB target identification, preventing unambiguous pharmacologic validation of endogenous CBL.
NX-1607 was tested preclinically during the final 16 of 20 Western-diet weeks, not as reversal after 20 weeks of established disease; no human atherosclerosis efficacy was assessed.
Mouse NX-1607 measurements found no reported ALT/AST liver-toxicity signal but did report lower white blood cells and lymphocytes, so safety is not established.

key_findings.claim: KIF13B expression is lower in advanced human arterial and carotid lesions and in progressing mouse plaques.
key_findings.context: Human findings are associative, not evidence that manipulating KIF13B changes human atherosclerosis.

evidence.label: GSE40231
evidence.value: 40 non-atherosclerotic and 40 atherosclerotic arterial-wall samples showed lower KIF13B in atherosclerotic tissue.

evidence.label: Human carotid tissue
evidence.value: Early n=6 and advanced n=6 lesions showed lower KIF13B protein in advanced plaques, with macrophage co-localization.

evidence.label: Mouse progression
evidence.value: Ldlr-deficient mice, n=6 per group, showed lower plaque KIF13B after 20 versus 12 weeks of Western diet.

key_findings.source_locator: Results: The expression of KIF13B is negatively correlated with the progression of atherosclerosis in patients and mice; Figure 1 and Supplementary Figure S1.

key_findings.claim: Global Kif13b loss worsened experimental atherosclerosis in Ldlr-deficient mice, but circulating lipids also increased in that model.
key_findings.context: The global Ldlr-deficient comparison does not isolate a lipid-independent mechanism; Apoe-background observations did not show the same lipid effect.

evidence.label: Ldlr model
evidence.value: After 12 weeks of Western diet, control versus global Kif13b-deficient Ldlr-deficient mice had n=6 mice per group; lesions and circulating total cholesterol and triglycerides increased with Kif13b loss.

evidence.label: Plaque phenotype
evidence.value: Necrotic-core area rose up to approximately twofold, CD68-positive macrophage infiltration more than threefold, and apoptotic-cell accumulation increased.

evidence.label: Apoe background
evidence.value: Worsened plaques were also reported in the Apoe-deficient background without the same circulating-lipid change.

key_findings.source_locator: Results: Deletion of Kif13b in Ldlr−/− mice exacerbates atherosclerosis; Figure 2 and Supplementary Figure S2.

key_findings.claim: Single-cell and macrophage analyses implicated altered macrophage states with lower Kif13b during experimental atherosclerosis.
key_findings.context: The study-generated aortic single-cell comparison pooled five mice into one library per genotype; Results and Figure 3E disagree on diet duration, so no single definitive duration is assigned.

evidence.label: GSE155513
evidence.value: Figure 3 uses one single-cell library at each 8-week and 26-week high-fat-diet time point; macrophage abundance rose and Kif13b reduction was prominent in macrophages.

evidence.label: Study-generated single-cell
evidence.value: Five aortas were pooled per genotype into one library, yielding 14 clusters and eight cell types; Cd80-positive, Il1b-positive, Spp1-positive and Cd206-positive macrophage states were emphasized, with Kif13b loss associated with fewer Cd206-positive and more Il1b-positive and Spp1-positive states.

evidence.label: Independent observations
evidence.value: GSE215103 Apoe-deficient macrophage reanalysis and ox-LDL-treated BMDM and THP-1 experiments also showed lower KIF13B.

key_findings.source_locator: Results: Kif13b deficiency primarily affects macrophage dynamics in mouse atherosclerosis; Figure 3.

key_findings.claim: Myeloid conditional deletion and Kif13b-deficient bone-marrow transfer worsened plaque phenotypes without corresponding plasma-lipid changes in their mouse models.
key_findings.context: These results support a lipid-independent myeloid or hematopoietic contribution in the tested models, not a macrophage-exclusive or proven human causal effect.

evidence.label: Lyz2-Cre model
evidence.value: Kif13b-floxed controls n=9 versus Lyz2-Cre;Kif13b-floxed mice n=6 after AAV8-PCSK9 and 12 weeks of Western diet; lesions, necrotic core, macrophages and apoptotic cells increased without material total-cholesterol, triglyceride or lipoprotein differences.

evidence.label: Bone-marrow transfer
evidence.value: Ldlr-deficient recipients of control versus Kif13b-deficient donor marrow, n=6 per group after 12 weeks of Western diet, showed worse plaque outcomes without plasma-lipid change.

key_findings.source_locator: Results: Myeloid-specific deletion of Kif13b aggravates atherosclerosis in a lipid-independent manner; Figure 4 and Supplementary Figures S3–S4.

key_findings.claim: Kif13b-deficient macrophages had impaired efferocytosis and reduced MERTK protein; restoring MERTK in deficient BMDMs improved efferocytosis.
key_findings.context: The genetic rescue was a macrophage cell experiment, not a demonstrated in vivo MERTK therapy or human rescue.

evidence.label: Transcriptomics
evidence.value: Wild-type and knockout BMDM RNA-seq n=3 per group and apoptotic-cell co-incubation RNA-seq n=3 per group nominated efferocytosis pathways.

evidence.label: Functional phenotype
evidence.value: BMDM efferocytosis assays n=5 per group and MERTK immunofluorescence n=10 per group implicated lower MERTK among evaluated efferocytosis proteins; in vivo conditional and marrow-transfer models also had impaired efferocytosis.

evidence.label: MERTK restoration
evidence.value: MERTK restoration in Kif13b-deficient BMDMs improved efferocytosis; western blot n=3 per group and efferocytosis rescue n=10 per group.

key_findings.source_locator: Results: Loss of Kif13b inhibits MERTK-mediated macrophage efferocytosis; Figure 5.

key_findings.claim: The KIF13B–ITCH–CBL–MERTK data support post-translational MERTK regulation, while the exact proposed ITCH-mediated CBL degradation step remains incompletely demonstrated.
key_findings.context: CBL is the endogenous gene/protein investigated; CBLB is distinct. Unchanged Mertk mRNA argues against a transcriptional explanation of lower MERTK protein in this experiment.

evidence.label: MERTK turnover
evidence.value: Mertk mRNA was unchanged in compared BMDMs n=3 per group; in THP-1 knockdown cells MERTK protein fell to about 40% at 16 hours of cycloheximide chase.

evidence.label: Protein mechanism
evidence.value: Proteasome inhibitor MG132 at 10 µM, but not chloroquine at 10 µM, blocked MERTK loss; MERTK ubiquitination and CBL protein increased with KIF13B loss.

evidence.label: ITCH interaction and rescue
evidence.value: KIF13B and ITCH co-immunoprecipitated, ITCH fell with KIF13B loss, and ITCH overexpression in deficient BMDMs reversed higher CBL and lower MERTK; direct proof of each proposed ITCH-to-CBL degradation step is incomplete.

evidence.label: Human association
evidence.value: Advanced human plaque tissues n=6 per group showed lower KIF13B, ITCH and MERTK and higher CBL; this is associative.

key_findings.source_locator: Results: KIF13B decreases CBL-mediated ubiquitination of MERTK by interacting with itch in macrophages; Figure 6.

key_findings.claim: NX-1607 improved MERTK and efferocytosis phenotypes in macrophages and reduced atherosclerotic phenotypes in mice; its target identity does not unambiguously validate endogenous CBL.
key_findings.context: The article calls NX-1607 a CBL inhibitor, while external authoritative drug-development sources identify it as a CBL-B/CBLB inhibitor; CBL and CBLB are distinct genes. These are preclinical rescue results, not human atherosclerosis treatment efficacy.

evidence.label: Macrophage assays

works.title: Advancing predictive markers in lung adenocarcinoma: A machine learning-based immunotherapy prognostic prediction signature
review_topics: Validation leakage in molecular survival models

supports: Description of the reported 13-gene Lasso-plus-SuperPC development procedure and 101 candidate combinations.
The text-and-figure-consistent TCGA training AUCs, explicitly labelled as apparent development-cohort performance.
A source-based distinction between survival-defined discovery groups, prognostic modeling and computational drug-response inference.
does_not_establish: An independently validated predictor of RECIST response or differential benefit from immunotherapy.
Prospective clinical utility or improved outcomes from IPPS-guided treatment.
Unbiased external performance after gene and algorithm selection using the same GEO cohorts.
A reconciled OAK/POPLAR denominator or a resolved GSE31210 AUC estimate.
Experimental drug efficacy or causal functions of the model genes.

limitations: The study is retrospective. Survival-based gene selection used all six TCGA/GEO cohorts, and five GEO cohorts were reused to choose the algorithm. Their results cannot be treated as untouched external validation.

Methods 2.1 states 577 OAK/POPLAR LUAD cases, while Results 3.1 and Figure 1D state a selected 296. The retrieved version does not sufficiently specify the full filtering relationship; no reconciled or pooled denominator is asserted.
Results 3.1 and Figure 1D use OS >12 months and OS <6 months but name the groups CR/PR and PD/SD. Survival strata do not establish objective response categories or differential immunotherapy benefit.
GSE31210 AUCs differ between Results 3.2 (0.67, 0.76, 0.72 at 1, 3, 5 years) and Figure 2L (0.67, 0.73, 0.75). Neither series is adopted as a verified performance estimate.
The TCGA AUCs quoted here are apparent training-cohort estimates. Individual participant data and code were not reanalysed, and no uncertainty interval is invented.
Drug-response analyses are computational. The Discussion uses experimental language, but Methods 2.4 and Results 3.7 describe inference from drug-sensitivity databases.

The author-uploaded publisher-layout text was readable publicly on ResearchGate, and Figures 1 and 2 were visually checked there. Direct PDF download was blocked in this environment; the archived source fingerprint identifies the acquired web transcription, not PDF bytes. No claim is based on an unseen supplementary result.

key_findings.claim: The reported IPPS contains 13 genes and uses Lasso plus SuperPC selected from 101 candidate combinations.
key_findings.context: Retrospective development in TCGA-LUAD. Candidate-gene survival screening included TCGA and five GEO cohorts; selection of the final algorithm used the mean C-index in those same five GEO cohorts.
key_findings.source_locator: Methods 2.2, author-uploaded publisher-layout pp. 2-3; Results 3.1-3.2, pp. 3-5; Figure 1D-E; Figure 2A.

key_findings.claim: The article reports TCGA training-cohort AUCs of 0.80, 0.79 and 0.78 for 1-, 3- and 5-year survival.
key_findings.context: These are apparent performance estimates in the TCGA development cohort, not independent external or prospective validation. The GSE31210 text-versus-figure discrepancy is excluded from performance claims.
key_findings.source_locator: Results 3.2, author-uploaded publisher-layout p. 5; Figure 2H, p. 4. Text and displayed TCGA panel agree.

key_findings.claim: The initial OAK/POPLAR comparison used overall-survival extremes and does not by itself establish an objective immunotherapy-response classifier.
key_findings.context: Figure 1D and Results 3.1 define groups by survival greater than 12 months or less than 6 months, while labelling them CR/PR and PD/SD. Those labels must not be treated as verified RECIST response classifications.
key_findings.source_locator: Results 3.1 and Figure 1D, author-uploaded publisher-layout p. 3; compare Methods 2.1, p. 2.

key_findings.claim: The drug-sensitivity analysis generates computational treatment hypotheses rather than observations of drug benefit in patients.
key_findings.context: The Methods names oncoPredict and pRRophetic, and Results 3.7 uses CTRP and PRISM drug-sensitivity resources. No new drug-treatment experiment is established by this analysis.
key_findings.source_locator: Methods 2.4, author-uploaded publisher-layout pp. 2-3; Results 3.7, p. 7; Discussion, pp. 10-12. No compound-specific effect estimate is reproduced.

works.title: Assessing personalized molecular portraits underlying endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition within pulmonary arterial hypertension

supports: PAH-associated endothelial transcriptional heterogeneity and computationally inferred EndMT-related expression programs.
A candidate two-gene PETS classifier with internal test-set performance under the reported dataset and analysis procedure.
Selected expression changes in hypoxic endothelial experimental systems.
does_not_establish: Direct lineage-tracing proof that the inferred trajectory is an in vivo cell-fate conversion.
A causal molecular mechanism from RARRES2 or TC2N to PAH or EndMT.
An independently externally validated or prospective diagnostic test, or demonstrated detection of early disease.
A validated serum PETS assay: the score was derived from transcriptomic expression, so discussion of serum translation remains a hypothesis.
Clinical efficacy or safety of chemerin/CMKLR1-targeted therapy, or any PETS-guided treatment benefit.

limitations: Human datasets are retrospective and the single-cell analysis has few donor samples; thousands of cells do not imply thousands of independent patients.
Trajectory inference, pathway scoring, ligand-receptor inference and co-expression are computational associations, not direct causal mechanisms.

The machine-learning testing subset is an internal split of GSE117261 and was also used to compare the nine algorithms and select the preferred model. Reported performance may therefore be optimistic. No untouched final test set, independent external clinical validation or prospective validation was established.
PETS is based on transcript expression. Discussion of serum-marker applications should not be read as a validated blood test.
Main text reports 602 EC3 marker genes, but the retrieved original Table S4 contains 604 distinct gene rows. This unresolved ancillary count difference is not silently harmonized.

A Results sentence describes lower incoming and higher outgoing communications but labels the role change in the opposite direction; no sender/receiver direction claim is carried into this evidence page.
A main-text sentence refers to MSRB1 while the candidate list and primer list use MSRB3. The page avoids drawing a gene-specific conclusion from that inconsistent sentence.
Targeted expression experiments do not demonstrate a beneficial intervention. Experimental sample sizes and fold-change values are not invented from plots.

populations: US NHANES adults aged at least 20 years

supports: Survey-weighted associations of LE8 and its subscores with PHQ-9-defined depressive symptoms in the selected 2007–2012 sample.
The depression-specific counts and estimates that agree across the abstract, Results and Table 2.
does_not_establish: That interventions improving LE8 prevent or treat depression or anxiety.
A causal direction between cardiovascular health and depressive symptoms.
Resolved anxiety event counts or effect estimates; these remain excluded.
Prospective depression prediction or psychiatric diagnosis by LE8.

limitations: Unresolved anxiety conflict: Abstract Results reports 2,947 anxiety participants and OR 0.78 (95% CI 0.75–0.81), whereas Results §3.1 reports 3,326 and Results §3.3/Table 2 give OR 0.80 (0.77–0.82). This page does not choose between these values; all anxiety estimates and anxiety-based conclusions are excluded. The discrepancy has not been declared corrected.
Cross-sectional associations do not determine temporal order, causality or efficacy of a cardiovascular-health intervention.
PHQ-9 ≥10 identifies depressive symptoms for this analysis and is not equivalent to an independently adjudicated psychiatric diagnosis.
Complete-data selection, self-reported behaviors and residual confounding can affect associations.
Supplementary subgroup/sensitivity results and spline plots are outside the independently verified quantitative claim set.

works.title: Associations between magnesium depletion score and depression among individuals aged 20 to 60 years
works.journal: Journal of Trace Elements in Medicine and Biology
review_topics: Magnesium depletion proxies and depressive symptoms
Medication and renal-function components in cross-sectional nutritional scores

supports: Reported survey-weighted MDS–PHQ-9 prevalence-odds associations in the included adults aged 20–60 years.
Definition of the proxy score, questionnaire outcome, analytic denominator and covariate-adjustment set in the main article.
Descriptive assessment of score categories, components, spline nonlinearity and subgroup interactions within the same survey sample.
does_not_establish: That magnesium depletion causes depression, or that lowering MDS or magnesium supplementation prevents or treats depression.
A validated clinical diagnosis, depression screening rule, individual prognosis or treatment threshold derived from MDS.
Direct measurement of serum or whole-body magnesium, or proof that magnesium mediates the observed medication associations.
Proof of linearity from P=0.084, identical effects across subgroups, or statistical significance in every subgroup.
Numerical results from Supplementary Tables 1–2, which were referenced by the paper but not obtained for this audit.

limitations: The cross-sectional design cannot establish temporal direction; reverse causation and residual confounding remain possible (Discussion, p. 5).
MDS combines medication use, kidney function and drinking behavior; it is not a biochemical magnesium measurement, and serum-magnesium comparison was unavailable (Methods 2.3; Discussion, p. 5).
PHQ-9 at least 10 is the study's questionnaire-based outcome, not an independently adjudicated clinical diagnosis (Methods 2.2).

Participants with specified missing data were excluded. The main text reports use of recommended NHANES weights but does not identify the exact weight variable, pooled-weight construction or a missing-data imputation procedure; no participant-level reanalysis is claimed (Fig. 1; Methods 2.1 and 2.5).
High MDS values were uncommon: scores 3, 4 and 5 contained 325, 41 and 2 participants and were pooled. High-score and subgroup estimates are correspondingly imprecise (Methods 2.3; Tables 2 and 4).
Supplementary Tables 1–2 were not available for this audit. Dietary-threshold specifications and alternative-category sensitivity estimates from those files are not presented as verified results.
Figure 2's caption uses beneficial-threshold language, but the design and results do not establish a beneficial or clinical intervention threshold. The nonlinearity P value does not prove linearity.
Generalization beyond the included US adult survey population requires independent evidence.

key_findings.claim: The pooled NHANES 2005–2018 cross-sectional analysis included 18,247 adults aged 20–60 years; 1,753 met the study's PHQ-9 threshold of at least 10.
key_findings.context: These are unweighted participant counts after the stated exclusions. PHQ-9 reflects self-reported symptoms in the preceding two weeks; the threshold classification is not an independently confirmed clinical diagnosis or incident depression outcome.
key_findings.source_locator: Publisher PDF p. 2, Methods 2.1–2.2 and Fig. 1; pp. 3–4, Table 1.

key_findings.claim: MDS was a 0–5 score assembled from diuretic use, proton pump inhibitor use, reduced estimated glomerular filtration rate and heavy drinking.
key_findings.context: The score is an operational proxy assembled from medication, renal-function and alcohol variables. This study did not measure or validate whole-body magnesium deficiency against serum magnesium. A higher score must not be described as a directly measured magnesium concentration.

evidence.label: renal component
evidence.value: 1 point for eGFR between 60 and 90; 2 points below 60 mL/min/1.73 m²

evidence.value: 1 point; more than 1 drink/day for women or 2 drinks/day for men

key_findings.source_locator: Publisher PDF p. 2, Methods 2.3; p. 5, Discussion limitations.

key_findings.claim: In survey-weighted Model 3, each one-point higher MDS was associated with higher odds of PHQ-9-defined depression: OR 1.15, 95% CI 1.04–1.26, P=0.0100.
key_findings.context: Model 3 adjusted for age, sex, race/ethnicity, education, marital status, BMI, smoking, diabetes and dietary energy, calcium and magnesium intake. This adjusted prevalence-odds association is neither a prospective risk estimate nor an effect of changing magnesium status.
key_findings.source_locator: Publisher PDF p. 3, Methods 2.5; p. 4, Results 3.2 and Table 2, continuous MDS row and footnote a.

key_findings.claim: Relative to MDS 0, Model 3 ORs were 1.03 (95% CI 0.87–1.21) for MDS 1, 1.41 (1.12–1.78) for MDS 2, and 1.58 (1.06–2.35) for MDS at least 3.
key_findings.context: MDS 1 did not show a statistically significant association. The highest category contained only 368 participants, including 71 with PHQ-9 at least 10; sparse high scores limit precision and do not define a clinical screening or treatment threshold.
key_findings.source_locator: Publisher PDF p. 4, Table 1 continuation, MDS rows; Table 2, Model 3 categorical MDS rows and footnote b.

key_findings.claim: The component analysis reported an association for proton pump inhibitor use in Model 3: OR 2.24, 95% CI 1.78–2.80, P<0.0001.
key_findings.context: Diuretic use, heavy drinking and the renal-function categories had confidence intervals crossing 1 in the same model. These component estimates do not establish medication-induced depression, magnesium mediation, or benefit from stopping a prescribed medication.
key_findings.source_locator: Publisher PDF p. 5, Table 3, Model 3 component rows and footnote a; p. 4, Results 3.2.

key_findings.claim: The restricted cubic spline analysis reported P=0.084 for nonlinearity.
key_findings.context: The test did not detect nonlinearity at the paper's 0.05 significance level; this is not proof that the relationship is linear. Figure 2's wording about a beneficial threshold is not adopted as a clinical claim, and no numerical threshold is extracted from the curve.
key_findings.source_locator: Publisher PDF p. 3, Methods 2.5; p. 4, Results 3.2; p. 5, Fig. 2 and its caption.

key_findings.claim: All reported subgroup interaction P values in Table 4 exceeded 0.05.
key_findings.context: Failure to detect interaction does not show that every subgroup estimate is statistically significant, identical or clinically useful. Several subgroup confidence intervals cross 1, and some are wide; these stratified analyses are not independent external validation.
key_findings.source_locator: Publisher PDF p. 3, Methods 2.5; p. 4, Results 3.3; p. 6, Table 4, interaction column and footnote a.

works.title: Causal Associations Between the Gut Microbiome and Aortic Aneurysm: A Mendelian Randomization Study

supports: The stated MiBioGen and FinnGen data-source design and AA/AAA estimates printed in main Table 1.
Different uncertainty across MR estimators for the same microbial trait and outcome.
does_not_establish: Benefits from changing the microbiome, probiotics, antibiotics or aneurysm-prevention treatment.
A validated screening biomarker, patient-level risk score or clinical threshold.
Proof of absent pleiotropy, valid instruments, or independently reproduced supplementary sensitivity and full multiple-testing results.
A resolved TAA endpoint definition or reconciled screen-wide microbial-taxon count.

limitations: The TAA Methods definition uses thoracoabdominal rather than thoracic outcomes; TAA-specific findings are excluded pending clarification.
The retained-taxon total is stated as 196, while Results category counts sum to 195; neither is presented as a reconciled screen-wide count.

Bonferroni correction is described by taxonomic level, but equation images and supplements were unavailable. Main-table estimates are reported as author-selected associations, not an independently reproduced screen-wide significance claim.
Alternative estimator intervals do not uniformly exclude the null; MR estimates remain assumption-dependent.
The exposure GWAS is multi-ethnic and the outcome source is Finnish. Portability, population structure and sample overlap require consideration; overlap was not quantified here.
Supplementary MR-PRESSO, Steiger, leave-one-out and instrument tables were not independently inspected. Non-significant diagnostic tests would not prove the absence of pleiotropy.
No intervention, prospective diagnostic validation or clinical treatment benefit was tested.

key_findings.claim: The study paired microbial genetic instruments with separate AA and AAA outcome summary statistics.

review_topics: Management of rare esophageal mesenchymal tumors
Selection bias in endoscopic and surgical case series

supports: The reported 23-patient case series and its mutually exclusive treatment allocations.

does_not_establish: Superior safety, survival or oncologic equivalence of endoscopy versus surgery.

A causal effect of imatinib or any procedure on recurrence or survival.
Prospective, multicenter or externally validated outcomes.
A reconciled 2023 enrollment cutoff or corrected mitotic-index category.

limitations: The study is retrospective and includes 23 patients at one center. Treatment was chosen by experienced clinicians on the basis of tumor size, location, origin and growth pattern, creating strong selection differences between treatment groups.

No randomized comparison, adjusted treatment-effect estimate or external validation establishes superiority or oncologic equivalence. The discussion’s procedural suggestions are not independently validated selection rules.
The abstract and Methods 2.1 specify January 2017 to August 2023, whereas Results 3.1 says January 2017 to December 2023. No exact corrected end date is adopted.
Results 3.2 describes the highest mitotic-index category as >5/50 HPF, while Table 2 labels it >10/50 HPF. This category is excluded from the quantitative findings rather than silently corrected.

The manuscript discusses an earlier procedure and suspected recurrence in patient No. 21 without the original postoperative pathology. It is not used to derive an additional event rate, survival curve or effect estimate.

Postoperative adverse-event counts and follow-up are reported observations in small selected groups. No unreported confidence interval, standardized quality-of-life score or recurrence-rate estimate is generated.

The complete six-page publisher-layout PDF was reviewed. It contains no identified supplementary-results appendix or supplementary-file citation needed for the findings reproduced here; this does not assert that no supplementary resource exists elsewhere.
