works.title: Plasma Olink Proteomics Reveals Novel Biomarkers for Prediction and Diagnosis in Dilated Cardiomyopathy with Heart Failure

supports: A predefined 92-protein cardiovascular Olink panel detected differential plasma protein abundance between the studied DCM-HF and healthy-control groups.
Thirteen proteins showed marked higher abundance in the Olink discovery analysis and remained significant after FDR correction.
SPP1, IGFBP7, F11R, CHI3L1 and PLAUR showed directionally consistent higher plasma levels in an independent local ELISA cohort.
The corresponding five-gene expression panel showed diagnostic discrimination across three external human cardiac transcriptomic datasets.
Several DCM-HF-associated plasma proteins were correlated with clinical indicators including NT-proBNP, LVEF, CRP and eGFR in the studied cohort.
Functional-enrichment and protein-interaction analyses provide biological hypotheses involving inflammatory, remodeling and related processes.
The five prioritized markers constitute candidates for larger biomarker-validation studies.
does_not_establish: That the Olink analysis provides an unbiased whole-proteome survey; it used a predefined targeted cardiovascular panel.
That the 13 differentially abundant proteins cause DCM-HF or directly determine disease severity.
That SPP1, IGFBP7, F11R, CHI3L1 or PLAUR are clinically validated diagnostic tests for DCM-HF.
That external cardiac transcriptomic evaluation constitutes independent plasma-proteomic replication.
That ROC discrimination in existing case-control/transcriptomic datasets predicts who will develop DCM-HF prospectively.
That the five-marker panel has demonstrated incremental clinical utility over echocardiography, cardiac MRI, NT-proBNP, troponin, or standard diagnostic assessment.
That correlation, GO/KEGG enrichment or PPI-network analysis establishes a causal molecular mechanism.
That any of the identified proteins is a validated therapeutic target or that biomarker-guided treatment improves clinical outcomes.
That this publication generated original mouse-model evidence; the Methods and Results do not describe an animal experiment.

limitations: The Olink discovery cohort was small, with 20 DCM-HF patients and 18 healthy controls.
The Olink assay was a predefined 92-protein cardiovascular panel rather than an unbiased whole-proteome measurement.
The local discovery and ELISA analyses were cross-sectional and do not establish prospective incident-disease prediction or longitudinal prognostic performance.

The external GEO evaluation used cardiac transcriptomic data rather than independent plasma-proteomic cohorts, so it supports corresponding gene-expression discrimination rather than direct protein-level replication.
Article-reported sample counts for the external GEO datasets differ from native or independently documented dataset composition, and the exact filtering logic is not fully specified.
Clinical correlations were exploratory and were not independently replicated for each protein-clinical-variable relationship.
GO/KEGG, STRING, Cytoscape and related analyses are computational and do not establish causal mechanisms or therapeutic efficacy.

The article reports ChiCTR2100051469, but publicly indexed registry information for that identifier appears to correspond to a different study; the linkage to this DCM-HF proteomics study is therefore unresolved.

Although the Introduction refers to human plasma and mouse models, the study Methods and Results do not describe an original animal experiment; mouse evidence discussed in the article derives from cited prior studies.

supports: Attribution of the mechanistic and competing-explanation framework to this 2024 narrative review.

Recognition that a conceptual diagram, case description and transgene assay answer different questions from a comparative incidence study.
does_not_establish: A new clinical cohort, prospective experiment, systematic review or meta-analysis.

That absence of a CAR transgene excludes every indirect treatment contribution, or that its presence identifies a unique oncogenic driver.

limitations: This is a selective narrative review without a reproducible systematic search, risk-of-bias assessment or pooled analysis. Its 2024 discussion is not a current clinical guideline.

Section 3.3 describes transgene-negative biopsies from 16 patients when citing reference 36. The cited study's Abstract, Results and Table 4 instead distinguish 13 affected patients, 16 tumor events and 11 available biopsies (DOI 10.1182/blood.2022015728; PMC9346960). No estimate using the review's conflated count is accepted here.

Section 3.3 uses 28 patients for reference 37. The cited ASH abstract describes 28 as the earlier population in its Background and 48 recipients in its long-term Results (DOI 10.1182/blood-2023-182817). Its event counts cannot be attached to the earlier denominator.

Figure 1B and the text's suggestion of no significant association are hypotheses, not an original statistical result. Lack of insertion in a recognized oncogene does not demonstrate absence of treatment-related malignant transformation.
The historical report counts and infusion total in Section 4 are not a matched numerator and denominator; no frequency is calculated. Product-specific reports cannot establish class-wide safety.
Statements about HHV-6, mature T-cell resistance and inflammatory carcinogenesis must not be promoted from discussion or extrapolation into demonstrated mechanisms of secondary malignancy in humans.
The article has 53 reference numbers, with the same Ghilardi publication repeated as references 13 and 53. These are not 53 independent studies.

works.title: Atherosclerotic plaque vulnerability quantification system for clinical and biological interpretability

supports: APVS discriminates several studied coronary and plaque pathological states in retrospective transcriptomic datasets.
APVSLevel is associated with plaque vulnerability, coronary stenosis severity, and MACE risk in the studied cohorts.
APVSLevel-high states exhibit stronger inflammatory, immune, procoagulant, and plaque-destabilizing molecular programs.
Single-cell datasets support APVSLevel as a molecular descriptor of vulnerable plaque biology and cellular-state remodeling.
APVS/APVSLevel can serve as a research framework for molecular stratification and mechanistic exploration of atherosclerotic plaque vulnerability.
does_not_establish: That APVS is a clinically approved diagnostic test for plaque vulnerability.
That the 14 APVS genes are causal drivers of plaque rupture.
That APVSLevel-guided treatment reduces myocardial infarction, mortality, or other clinical events.
That transcriptomic APVS/APVSLevel can replace coronary imaging, cardiac biomarkers, or standard clinical assessment.
That retrospective public-dataset validation is equivalent to prospective multicenter clinical validation.
That drug-response or signature-reversal analyses constitute therapeutic recommendations.

limitations: The study was based predominantly on retrospective public high-throughput datasets.
Prospective multicenter studies are required to confirm the biological and clinical interpretability of APVSLevel.
The APVS classifier requires further direct comparison with established clinical biomarkers.
The functions of many APVS-related molecules remain incompletely established and require additional in vivo and in vitro validation.
Incomplete clinical and molecular traits in source datasets may obscure associations between APVS and some relevant factors.

works.title: Smooth muscle cell fate decisions decipher a high-resolution heterogeneity within atherosclerosis molecular subtypes
review_topics: Smooth muscle cell heterogeneity in human plaque
Cell-state programs and molecular disease subtypes

biological_processes: vascular smooth muscle cell phenotypic switching

supports: Human coronary atherosclerotic plaques contain substantial transcriptional heterogeneity among vascular smooth muscle cells.
The analyzed SMC transcriptomes can be computationally organized into a pseudotime trajectory with five states and distinct cluster distributions.
A 1,072-gene fate-leader set and temporal expression modules summarize SMC state-associated transcriptional programs in these data.
SCFDS-based analysis identified three retrospective molecular subtypes with distinct DNA-repair, inflammatory/immune and stromal/ECM-associated profiles.
C2 was associated with greater coronary stenosis severity and C3 with lower severity in the discovery analysis.
The three-subtype expression-template structure was reproducible across five independent retrospective transcriptomic cohorts.
SCFDS can serve as a research framework for studying SMC-related molecular heterogeneity in atherosclerosis.
does_not_establish: That the nine SMC clusters are fixed biological lineages or clinically defined cell types.
That pseudotime directly observes individual human SMCs transforming longitudinally within the same lesion.
That all 1,072 fate-leader genes causally regulate SMC fate.
That C1, C2 and C3 are prospectively validated clinical diagnostic or prognostic classes.
That C2 causes coronary stenosis progression or that C3 causally protects against plaque progression or clinical events.
That pathway enrichment or inferred cell-composition differences prove the underlying mechanisms.
That retrospective NTP reproducibility is equivalent to prospective multicenter clinical validation.
That SCFDS-guided treatment improves myocardial infarction, mortality or other clinical outcomes.
That the therapeutic hypotheses discussed by the authors constitute validated treatment recommendations.

limitations: The study was primarily computational and cannot fully recapitulate the diversity of developmental states or directly demonstrate longitudinal SMC lineage transitions in human plaques.
The plaque single-cell analysis was based on four human donors, limiting direct generalization of cell-state frequencies.
All samples used for subtype analyses were retrospective; prospective multicenter clinical validation was not performed.
NTP validation demonstrates retrospective expression-template reproducibility rather than prospective diagnostic, prognostic or treatment-predictive performance.
Pathway enrichment, xCell and related computational inference generate biological hypotheses but do not establish causal mechanisms.

The article contains inconsistencies in sample/cohort enumeration and one external-cohort accession identifier; counts and dataset provenance should therefore be preserved explicitly rather than silently reconciled.

supports: Shared transcriptional signals across independently profiled COVID-19 and HF datasets.
Inflammatory and innate-immune pathway enrichment and network prioritization of TLR-associated genes.

Computational TF/miRNA and candidate-compound hypothesis generation.
Hypothesis generation around gut-heart and LPS biology, without direct measurement of microbiome or LPS.
does_not_establish: Germline genetic correlation, inherited susceptibility, GWAS evidence, Mendelian randomization, or genetic causality.

Prospective clinical validation, diagnostic accuracy, or prognostic utility of a five-gene panel.
Experimentally demonstrated TF/miRNA regulation or direct measurement of gut microbiome dysbiosis, intestinal permeability, or circulating LPS.
Proteomic evidence or therapeutic efficacy of glutathione, muramyl dipeptide, or another intervention.

limitations: Human evidence was assembled retrospectively from heterogeneous public expression datasets; no dedicated simultaneous COVID-19 and HF cohort or prospective clinical validation was reported.

PPI, TF/miRNA and drug-signature findings are computational or database-derived and lack direct causal perturbation validation.

No proteomics, candidate-compound treatment experiment, or demonstrated therapeutic efficacy for glutathione or muramyl dipeptide was reported.

all_questions.question: What data underpin the DCM network subtypes?
all_questions.answer: Four public myocardial expression datasets were analyzed. Table 1 reports 245 DCM and 174 control samples in total. These are sample counts; the evidence page does not present them as a verified unique-patient total.

all_questions.question: How were network perturbations constructed?
all_questions.answer: The analysis ranked genes within each sample, calculated rank differences for interacting genes and compared those differences with a control-derived reference. Selected perturbation edges were then used for clustering.

all_questions.question: How many molecular subtypes were identified?
all_questions.answer: The selected solution comprised EPS1, EPS2 and EPS3. Their reported frequencies ranged from 43.2-52.5%, 40.0-44.2% and 7.5-13.5%, respectively, across the analyzed datasets.

all_questions.question: Were the immune differences measured directly in individual cells?
all_questions.answer: No. Immune-related scores were inferred from bulk gene-expression profiles using ssGSEA. Those associations are useful for generating hypotheses but are not direct cell counts or proof of immune causation.

all_questions.question: Does EPS1 prove that immunoadsorption will work for a patient?
all_questions.answer: No. EPS1 expression matched the responder profile in a retrospective Submap analysis. A trial of subtype-guided treatment, with prospectively specified outcomes, would be needed to establish clinical benefit.

all_questions.question: What did the AC16-cell experiment validate?
all_questions.answer: It checked the direction of eight genes selected from overlapping EPS1-versus-control and DCM-versus-control contrasts. Three increased and five decreased after angiotensin-II treatment. It does not validate all three subtypes or their treatment responses.

all_questions.question: Can the subtype frequencies be used as population prevalence estimates?
all_questions.answer: No. They describe selected public myocardial datasets and the reported analysis procedure. They are not estimates from a population-based DCM sampling frame.

all_questions.question: What experimental systems were actually studied?
all_questions.answer: Controlled chemical solutions and mice were studied. The main atherosclerosis model uses male ApoE-/- mice after 16 weeks of high-fat feeding; the study does not report a cell-culture validation experiment or a human cohort.

all_questions.question: How does ReP respond to superoxide and glutathione?
all_questions.answer: The authors assign the optical switching to catechol-based oxidation by superoxide and reduction by GSH. Superoxide increases the 740 nm PA response and GSH attenuates it; three alternating cycles are shown in solution.

all_questions.question: What quantitative PA calibration was reported?
all_questions.answer: The displayed superoxide PA calibration spans 0 to 80 micromolar and has R-squared 0.977. The GSH panel spans 0 to 300 micromolar and has R-squared 0.982. The separate superoxide absorption titration extends to 125 micromolar; the ranges must not be conflated.

all_questions.question: Was an absolute or ratiometric plaque redox measurement validated?
all_questions.answer: The displayed animal metric is relative PA intensity in an aortic-region ROI at 740 nm. Although introductory text uses ratiometric language, the figures do not define a validated two-wavelength ratio or convert animal signal into an absolute plaque superoxide concentration.

all_questions.question: Which inflammatory and treatment conditions were tested in mice?
all_questions.answer: The main groups are AS plus PBS, AS plus LPS, and AS plus LPS followed by dexamethasone, with n=3 per group. LPS is 50 micrograms in 50 microliters PBS intranasally on days 0 and 1. Dexamethasone is 2 mg/kg/day intraperitoneally from day 2 to day 8; ReP is 300 microliters at 200 micromolar via tail vein.

all_questions.question: What did histology add to the imaging comparison?
all_questions.answer: Lung wet/dry measurements and H&E support the pulmonary-inflammatory model. Plaque CD68, caspase-3 and Masson staining show group differences; the Fig. 6 percentages are descriptive annotations without supplied per-animal uncertainty or inferential tests.

all_questions.question: Does the study show fewer ruptures or clinical treatment benefit?
all_questions.answer: No rupture-prevention or human cardiovascular-event trial is reported. PA signal and tissue staining in these mouse groups do not establish dexamethasone benefit in patients, clinical diagnostic performance or event prediction.

all_questions.question: What safety conclusion can be supported?
all_questions.answer: The authors report seven-day body-weight observations and major-organ histology in mice. The independent tolerability n is not supplied; these descriptive results do not establish chronic, repeated-dose or human safety.

all_questions.question: Which population and incident outcomes were analyzed?
all_questions.answer: The analytic cohort comprised 205,504 participants and 18,542 incident CVD events during an article-reported 13-year follow-up period. The analytic sample is not the entire UK Biobank recruitment population. The reported 13-year period is not described here as a mean or median follow-up.

all_questions.question: What does the allostatic-load score represent?
all_questions.answer: Allostatic load was operationalized using 12 baseline biomarkers with quartile-based risk scoring and a score range of 0–12. HDL and IGF-1 used the low-value risk direction. This biomarker score is not a direct measurement of psychological stress, a neuroendocrine response or an inflammatory intervention.

all_questions.question: What was the adjusted high-versus-zero AL association?
all_questions.answer: In adjusted Model 3, AL ≥6 versus AL = 0 was associated with incident CVD at HR 2.15 (95% CI 1.99–2.33). AL = 0 is the reference group. This relative hazard association is not a 115% absolute-risk increase or a treatment effect.

all_questions.question: What do the nonlinear and sensitivity analyses add?
all_questions.answer: The AL–CVD association was nonlinear, and the main text reported directionally similar results after excluding events in the first three years after baseline. No additional precise hazard ratios from supplementary tables are supplied here, and this sensitivity analysis does not fully exclude reverse causation.

all_questions.question: Does the mediation estimate establish prevention by lowering neutrophils?
all_questions.answer: Eight candidate mediators entered the correlation analysis; the neutrophil-count mediation estimate was 4.73%. This is model-based decomposition using baseline indicators, not a proven causal pathway or evidence that lowering neutrophils or an inflammatory marker prevents CVD.

all_questions.question: Which correspondence under this shared DOI is covered?
all_questions.answer: Only the letter signed by Mengyao Li, Ge Zhang and Xiaozhu Liu, indexed as PMID 41780015, is covered. Other letters and the trialists' reply are excluded.

all_questions.question: What does the 83% figure mean?
all_questions.answer: Among monotherapy patients who had stent thrombosis, the letter reports that 83% experienced it within 30 days. This is not the probability of thrombosis for every monotherapy patient.

all_questions.question: What further investigation do the authors propose?
all_questions.answer: They propose studying time-adaptive de-escalation, including platelet-function testing to inform transitions as ischemic and bleeding risks evolve.

all_questions.question: Can this letter establish a safe aspirin-withdrawal schedule?
all_questions.answer: No. It supplies interpretation and a research proposal, without a new randomized comparison or validated individualized stopping rule.

all_questions.question: What type of article is this?
all_questions.answer: It is a narrative Review Article synthesizing prior evidence. It reports no new experimental or clinical dataset, systematic study-selection workflow or pooled meta-analysis.

all_questions.question: Which circadian clock components are central to cardiovascular immune regulation?
all_questions.answer: The review centers on CLOCK-BMAL1, PER/CRY and REV-ERB/ROR feedback networks, including redox and epigenetic regulation; these are synthesized from prior work rather than tested as one new experiment.

all_questions.question: How does circadian disruption interact with NF-kB and NLRP3?
all_questions.answer: The review links clock and redox regulation with pattern-recognition receptor, NF-kB and NLRP3 inflammatory signaling, cytokines and chemokines. The underlying models are heterogeneous and do not establish one complete causal pathway in humans.

all_questions.question: Which immune cells show circadian trafficking or functional rhythms?
all_questions.answer: Prior evidence discussed for neutrophils, monocytes/macrophages, lymphocytes and dendritic cells indicates rhythmic numbers, trafficking or function, with phase and mechanism varying across species and tissues.

all_questions.question: Which cardiovascular diseases are discussed?
all_questions.answer: The review discusses atherosclerosis, stroke, ischemic heart disease and myocardial infarction, and heart failure, with hypertension considered in blood-pressure chronotherapy. Evidence strength differs across disease contexts.

all_questions.question: Does the review prove that REV-ERB agonists treat cardiovascular disease in humans?
all_questions.answer: No. REV-ERB agonist chronotherapy is discussed as mechanistic and preclinical rationale, not demonstrated human cardiovascular treatment efficacy.

all_questions.question: Should all antihypertensive medications be taken at bedtime?
all_questions.answer: No. Clinical evidence conflicts: Hygia and related studies reported bedtime-dosing benefits, while BedMed did not reproduce a cardiovascular-event benefit. The review does not support a universal bedtime recommendation.

all_questions.question: Does bedtime aspirin have proven myocardial infarction or stroke outcome benefit?
all_questions.answer: No large randomized trial cited by this review directly establishes reduced overall myocardial infarction or stroke incidence from bedtime aspirin dosing; physiological timing effects do not prove event reduction.

all_questions.question: Are SGLT2-inhibitor, colchicine, MRA or ARNI dosing times clinically established?
all_questions.answer: No. The review discusses these drug classes, but does not establish clinically validated optimal timing or universal cardiovascular outcome benefits for them.

all_questions.question: Is this a systematic review or meta-analysis?
all_questions.answer: No. The article reports no explicit systematic-search strategy, PRISMA study-selection workflow or quantitative meta-analysis; its 392 references are bibliography entries, not a systematic count of independent studies.

all_questions.question: What gaps remain before cardiovascular chronotherapy can become precision medicine?
all_questions.answer: Constitutive-versus-inducible model differences, immune-subpopulation and spatiotemporal heterogeneity, individualized rhythm variation and high-quality circadian-aware clinical trials remain important gaps.

all_questions.question: How many participants contributed to the analyses?
all_questions.answer: The UK Biobank analytic cohort contained 261,865 participants. The external hospital cohort initially contained 1,798 participants, but the fully adjusted external analysis used 328 complete cases, including 88 MACE outcomes. These populations and subsets should not be added into a synthetic study total.

all_questions.question: What does the TyG:eGFRcr-cys ratio combine?
all_questions.answer: It divides the triglyceride–glucose index by estimated GFR derived using both creatinine and cystatin C. It is intended to summarize metabolic and renal risk-marker information, rather than directly measure a causal process.

all_questions.question: What was the main prospective CVD association?
all_questions.answer: In fully adjusted Model 3, the highest ratio quartile had a CVD HR of 1.24 compared with the lowest quartile, with a 95% CI of 1.18–1.30. This is an observational hazard ratio.

all_questions.question: Were all cardiovascular outcomes significantly associated in the quartile comparison?
all_questions.answer: No. The highest-versus-lowest-quartile CHD HR was 1.30, while the stroke HR was 1.05 with a 95% CI of 0.96–1.16 and P=0.29. Outcome and exposure-contrast details must be preserved.

all_questions.question: What does external validation mean here?
all_questions.answer: It means that the ratio–MACE association was examined in an independent hospital cohort. The fully adjusted complete-case analysis was small and the confidence interval was wide; this does not establish a calibrated prediction model or improved clinical decision-making.

all_questions.question: Does the network analysis establish a pre-disease transition?
all_questions.answer: No. The analysis compared exposure-defined groups and was exploratory. It does not show that an individual crosses a validated early-warning threshold over time.

all_questions.question: Can the ratio replace established cardiovascular risk scores?
all_questions.answer: The article states that incremental discrimination and reclassification beyond established risk factors or scores were not evaluated. The ratio remains a candidate complementary marker requiring additional evaluation.

all_questions.question: What design rationale supports combining complementary learners in a clinical AI ensemble?
all_questions.answer: Choose complementary learners in relation to the clinical context rather than pursuing a single algorithm as universally optimal. The authors frame learner combination as a methodological design choice for clinical AI.

all_questions.question: How does the AI ensemble Perspective propose evaluating and selecting models across independent cohorts?
all_questions.answer: Evaluate and select models using aggregate evidence across independent cohorts. The Perspective recommends an evaluation strategy; it does not report executing these independent-cohort validations.

all_questions.question: Why should clinical AI feature attribution be considered alongside sensitivity analysis and calibration?
all_questions.answer: Interpret SHAP attributions as distribution-dependent and examine them alongside sensitivity analysis and calibration. The authors discuss robustness and interpretation constraints of feature attribution rather than identifying stable causal properties.

all_questions.question: Which deployment constraints does the AI ensemble Perspective identify for clinical translation?
all_questions.answer: Account for distribution shift, computational resources, standardization and clinical workflows when planning translation. These constraints define a future translation agenda rather than demonstrated clinical benefits.

all_questions.question: What problem does this correspondence address?
all_questions.answer: It addresses when multimodal cardiovascular AI has enough current and clinically relevant evidence to predict, and when it should defer.

all_questions.question: How does it define the role of deferral?
all_questions.answer: Deferral follows prespecified evidence-adequacy criteria and should trigger an alternative care pathway; it is not synonymous with calibration or high model confidence.

all_questions.question: Which evaluation conditions does it propose?
all_questions.answer: Five candidate conditions are complete inputs, a critical modality missing, natural co-missingness, temporal staleness and geographically or temporally external data.

all_questions.question: Does it report new model accuracy or a clinical trial?
all_questions.answer: No. It is a correspondence presenting conceptual proposals, with no new dataset or validated performance result.

all_questions.question: What happened to mutant PAPPA2 in the expression experiment?
all_questions.answer: At 48 hours after plasmid transfection, the three independent experiments showed lower mutant PAPPA2 protein in 293T cell lysates and culture supernatant, while the mRNA comparison was not statistically significant. This is an abundance result, not a direct protein half-life measurement.

all_questions.question: Which primary-cell treatment conditions support the fibrosis-associated finding?
all_questions.answer: Two donor-derived primary trabecular-meshwork lines were exposed for 48 hours to IGFBP5 at 100 ng/mL, PAPPA2 at 10 ng/mL, or their combination. PAPPA2 cotreatment attenuated the IGFBP5-associated protein and fluorescence responses. The reported 20 imaged cells per group per experiment are subsamples, not independent human donors.

all_questions.question: What did the mouse experiment measure, and did it reproduce the human variant?
all_questions.answer: At eight weeks, five mice per genotype were assessed. Pappa2 heterozygous and knockout mice had higher intraocular pressure and more trabecular Masson-positive staining than wild type. These are deficiency models, not mice carrying an engineered human p.Gly131Ala allele.

all_questions.question: Do these experiments validate a human glaucoma mutation or establish a treatment?
all_questions.answer: No. The cell and mouse findings provide experimental support for PAPPA2-IGFBP5 biology but do not establish population pathogenicity or human therapeutic benefit. Family-wide segregation and the reported pedigree denominator are not independently reconciled here, and no human therapeutic intervention was tested.

all_questions.question: What public-record problem does this Science Letter address?
all_questions.answer: The authors describe a gap between a previously reported human outcome and the registry or preclinical publication, and argue that directly related human protocols and major outcomes should remain visible in current public records. The case is contextual evidence from other sources, not a new study in this Letter.

all_questions.question: Why can an outdated registry matter in single-patient research?
all_questions.answer: An individual outcome may be the available human evidence. The Letter argues that families, clinicians, ethics committees and other researchers can rely on the public entry when judging continued testing and emerging risks.

all_questions.question: Does reporting to regulators ensure that the public record is updated?
all_questions.answer: The Letter distinguishes safety reports, trial registries and journal articles because their purposes and update schedules differ. Clinical information reaching an oversight body can still be absent from the public account of translation.

all_questions.question: Which changes do the authors propose for registries and preclinical papers?
all_questions.answer: They propose disclosure and updating of directly related human protocols before preclinical manuscript acceptance, reporting of treatment-emergent deaths and life-threatening events separately from causal assessment, links between preclinical papers and trial records, and dated notices for major later human outcomes.

all_questions.question: Does this Letter establish treatment causality or assign responsibility?
all_questions.answer: No. Its conclusion explicitly separates documenting subsequent human experience from assigning blame or settling causality. Its proposals concern reporting and governance, with no new clinical experiment or quantified treatment effect.

all_questions.question: What is ClockProCRC and how was it constructed?
all_questions.answer: ClockProCRC is a transcriptomic circadian-misalignment scoring framework. The study began with a 906-gene colon circadian reference and separately used CRC single-cell co-expression analysis to derive nine modules and a 559-gene four-module CTD signature. The ClockProCRC scoring Methods then applied expression-matched random-background correction to circadian rhythm disorder genes using 100 expression bins and 1,000 random samplings. The reviewed manuscript text does not establish that the 559 CTD genes are identical to the final scoring gene set.

all_questions.question: How large was the ClockProCRC study?
all_questions.answer: The Methods reports 3,758 samples across 35 public GEO datasets. The primary GSE166555 single-cell cohort comprised 25 tissue samples (13 CRC and 12 normal mucosa) and retained 94,683 cells after quality control. These are heterogeneous sample, tissue and cell counts and should not be interpreted as 3,758 unique human participants.

all_questions.question: Was ClockProCRC associated with colorectal-cancer progression and survival?
all_questions.answer: Yes, within the analyzed retrospective/public datasets. ClockProCRC increased across progression-related states from normal mucosa through adenoma/dysplasia and CRC to colorectal liver metastasis, and higher scores were associated with worse overall survival in GSE17537 (n=55; log-rank P<0.01). This is association evidence rather than prospective clinical validation.

all_questions.question: What did the single-cell analysis show about circadian misalignment and the CRC tumor microenvironment?
all_questions.answer: In GSE200997 and GSE196964, ClockProCRC-defined higher-disruption states were associated with enrichment of epithelial and plasma-cell populations, relative depletion of fibroblast/endothelial populations, and altered intercellular communication including stronger pro-inflammatory signaling patterns. These analyses identify state associations and do not by themselves prove causality.

all_questions.question: Why was SYNE1 prioritized in this study?
all_questions.answer: SYNE1 emerged from the CTD gene-regulatory-network analysis. Across 100 genetic-algorithm iterations, 61 recurrent regulatory axes were identified, and the NFATC2→SYNE1 relationship showed higher modeled regulatory strength in CRC (0.607; 95% CI 0.412-0.802) than in normal mucosa (-0.102; 95% CI -0.058-0.262). SYNE1 also showed circadian perturbation-associated expression/rhythmicity changes in independent datasets.

all_questions.question: What happened when SYNE1 was knocked down in colorectal-cancer cells?
all_questions.answer: In HCT116 and SW480 cells, siRNA-mediated SYNE1 knockdown reduced Transwell migration/invasion, reduced wound-healing migration and colony formation, increased E-cadherin and ZO-1, and decreased N-cadherin. These findings support an in-vitro functional role but do not establish in-vivo therapeutic efficacy.

all_questions.question: How did CLOCK knockdown, melatonin and the reported SYNE1 AUC relate to the circadian perturbation experiment?
all_questions.answer: CLOCK knockdown increased ClockProCRC and disrupted SYNE1 rhythmicity; melatonin partially restored the ClockProCRC-defined state and SYNE1 rhythmicity in CRC-cell experiments. The reported SYNE1 AUC of 0.915 refers specifically to discrimination of CLOCK-knockdown experimental conditions, not to CRC diagnosis or patient-level prediction.

all_questions.question: Are ClockProCRC or SYNE1 clinically validated for diagnosis, prognosis or treatment selection?
all_questions.answer: No. ClockProCRC has multicohort analytical and retrospective association evidence but lacks large prospective multicenter clinical validation and a universal clinical cutoff. SYNE1 has computational and in-vitro functional evidence but no SYNE1-directed animal efficacy or patient-treatment validation.

all_questions.question: Who was included in the analysis?
all_questions.answer: The final analytic cohort comprised 6,534 CHARLS participants aged at least 45 years without baseline CLMM. Baseline measurements were from 2011 and outcome ascertainment from 2015.

all_questions.question: What counted as cardiovascular–liver–metabolic multimorbidity?
all_questions.answer: Participants had to meet at least two criteria for CVD, type 2 diabetes, and LAP-based suspected MASLD at follow-up. The liver component was a surrogate phenotype, not universal imaging or histological confirmation.

all_questions.question: How strong was the association with CHG?
all_questions.answer: In the fully adjusted logistic model, the highest versus lowest CHG quartile had an OR of 1.64 with a 95% CI of 1.22–2.22. This is an observational odds ratio for the follow-up outcome.

all_questions.question: Did CHG-BMI perform better than CHG alone?
all_questions.answer: CHG-BMI had a stronger highest-versus-lowest-quartile association and the largest observed AUC among the compared indices. Its AUC of 0.643 was still modest and was evaluated in the analysis sample.

all_questions.question: Was this an externally validated clinical prediction model?
all_questions.answer: No. The article explicitly describes apparent, in-sample ROC evaluation without internal or external validation. Independent population validation and assessment beyond BMI and conventional risk factors are still needed.

all_questions.question: Did high CHG and high BMI interact statistically?
all_questions.answer: The jointly high group had greater follow-up CLMM odds than the low–low group, but the multiplicative interaction was not statistically significant. Joint association therefore does not establish synergy.

all_questions.question: Can these findings guide a treatment intended to prevent CLMM?
all_questions.answer: The study did not test an intervention. Observational associations and apparent discrimination do not establish that changing an index prevents disease or improves clinical decisions.

all_questions.question: What is the human evidence linking KIF13B to atherosclerotic plaque severity?
all_questions.answer: Paired carotid endarterectomy tissue and independent human transcriptomic and proteomic datasets showed lower KIF13B in more advanced or unstable plaque states, with prominent VSMC differences and lower collagen in advanced local plaque regions. These are associative human observations and do not establish that manipulating KIF13B changes plaque outcomes in patients.

all_questions.question: Did VSMC-specific Kif13b deletion cause worse atherosclerosis in mice?
all_questions.answer: In the tested male AAV8-PCSK9 model, VSMC-specific Kif13b deletion increased lesion burden, necrotic core, macrophage accumulation and apoptotic-cell signal and reduced collagen/plaque-stability features. No genotype difference in measured plasma total cholesterol or triglycerides was detected in the primary comparison.

all_questions.question: What did the single-cell experiment show, and were there five independent replicates per genotype?
all_questions.answer: The pooled aortic single-cell comparison associated KIF13B loss with reduced matrix/collagen programs and increased inflammatory VSMC-derived programs. Five mice were pooled into one single-cell library per genotype, so the design does not provide five independent scRNA-seq libraries per group.

all_questions.question: Why does this page not assign one definitive diet duration to all single-cell analyses?
all_questions.answer: The Results and Figure 5 describe the generated aortic single-cell experiment after 20 weeks of Western diet, whereas Figure 6 SCENIC and Figure 7 integrative captions reference 12 weeks. The evidence page preserves this source discrepancy instead of silently harmonizing it.

all_questions.question: How does KIF13B affect primary human vascular smooth muscle cells?
all_questions.answer: Under oxLDL, KIF13B knockdown reduced contractile/matrix features, collagen secretion and collagen-gel contraction and increased inflammatory features, while KIF13B overexpression produced reciprocal effects. These are in vitro primary-HASMC perturbation data, not human treatment outcomes.

all_questions.question: Is KLF4 functionally downstream of KIF13B?
all_questions.answer: In primary HASMC experiments, KIF13B loss increased KLF4, and concomitant KLF4 knockdown rescued the collagen-suppressive and inflammatory phenotype caused by KIF13B knockdown. This supports a downstream functional relationship in the tested cell system.

all_questions.question: What evidence supports the KIF13B-KCTD10-KLF4 mechanism?
all_questions.answer: KIF13B knockdown stabilized KLF4 in CHX/proteasome experiments and reduced KLF4 ubiquitination. Integrated analyses nominated KCTD10, co-IP supported KCTD10-KLF4 association, KCTD10 increased KLF4 ubiquitination, and KCTD10 overexpression rescued KIF13B-loss phenotypes. The study does not resolve how KIF13B itself controls KCTD10 abundance.

all_questions.question: Does Kenpaullone prove that KLF4 is a clinically validated treatment target for atherosclerosis?
all_questions.answer: No. Kenpaullone reduced KLF4 promoter activity/expression and rescued cellular and mouse phenotypes in this study, but the experiments were preclinical. Kenpaullone is also a pharmacologically nonselective kinase inhibitor rather than an established KLF4-selective clinical drug, and no human atherosclerosis treatment efficacy or safety was tested.

all_questions.question: How does this JCI study differ from the European Heart Journal KIF13B study?
all_questions.answer: The JCI study focuses on vascular smooth muscle cells and a KIF13B-KCTD10-KLF4 mechanism controlling matrix/inflammatory VSMC states. The European Heart Journal study focuses on macrophage KIF13B, MERTK-dependent efferocytosis and an ITCH/CBL regulatory network. Together they describe distinct cell-type-specific KIF13B mechanisms in experimental atherosclerosis.

all_questions.question: Which public datasets and repositories support this evidence page?
all_questions.answer: Key resources include study-generated mouse single-cell data GSE314838, human stable/unstable carotid plaque RNA-seq GSE120521, human plaque proteomics PXD062283, public spatial-transcriptomic evidence associated with GSE274572, the article's public methylation datasets, the JCI Supplemental Data, and the Supporting Data Values file.

all_questions.question: Which research directions does the cardiovascular AI Correspondence propose for multimodal models?
all_questions.answer: Develop multimodal AI along two directions: mechanism-oriented research and individualized digital twins. The authors propose complementary research directions rather than introduce a clinically validated digital twin product.

all_questions.question: How can imaging and molecular information support cardiovascular network and disease-subtyping hypotheses?
all_questions.answer: Integrate imaging and molecular information to formulate network and disease-subtyping hypotheses. Data integration and cited empirical examples are discussed as a basis for interpretation, not as new causal experiments in this Correspondence.

all_questions.question: What modeling approaches does the cardiovascular AI Correspondence discuss for patient-specific simulation?
all_questions.answer: Explore updateable physiological models, image-to-mesh workflows and treatment-scenario simulation. The simulation discussion concerns model design and possible scenarios, not observed human treatment effects.

all_questions.question: What requirements does the cardiovascular AI Correspondence identify for translating patient-specific models?
all_questions.answer: Address longitudinal data, computational resources, prospective evaluation, privacy and governance before clinical translation. These are stated development and evaluation requirements, not completed prospective clinical validation.

all_questions.question: How did the nine-gene ALS model perform externally?
all_questions.answer: The random forest signature reported AUC 1.00 in training, 0.91 internally, and 0.75 in independent GSE112680, reflecting lower transport performance; no prospective clinical impact test was performed.

all_questions.question: Does MR prove ABCA1 upregulation treats ALS?
all_questions.answer: No. IVW MR estimated an inverse association with ALS susceptibility (OR 0.93; 95% CI 0.87–0.99) under genetic instrument assumptions; that is not a drug intervention or demonstrated treatment benefit.

all_questions.question: How many people were in the serum cohort?
all_questions.answer: Fifteen ALS cases and fifteen controls (30 participants). The reported group comparison had P=0.006 but is too small to establish clinical diagnostic validity.

all_questions.question: Was serum ABCA1 associated with functional disability?
all_questions.answer: The reported ALSFRS-R total correlation r=-0.190, P=0.497 was not statistically significant; the evidence summary does not claim functional prediction.

all_questions.question: Is ABCA1 significantly upregulated in mouse spinal cord from day 70?
all_questions.answer: No. The supplied original Supplementary Table 14 reports mouse day-70 P=0.414 (adjusted P approximately 1). Stronger reported evidence appears on days 100 and 120; the published day-70 significant-onward phrase is inconsistent with its numbers.

all_questions.question: Are neutrophil and NK findings direct cell counts?
all_questions.answer: No. The reported associations come from ssGSEA immune-cell transcriptomic signatures and should not be interpreted as flow-cytometric cell-number measurements.

all_questions.question: How many participants and which outcomes were analyzed?
all_questions.answer: One analytic sample of 29,340 adults was used for both outcomes; Tables 2 and 3 list 5,433 hyperuricemia and 1,346 self-reported gout cases. These case counts must not be substituted for survey-weighted prevalence.

all_questions.question: Was every higher eGDR category significantly associated with less gout?
all_questions.answer: No. Table 3 Model 3 gives OR 0.81, 95% CI 0.63–1.04 and P=0.093 for 4–6 versus <4 mg/kg/min. Results §3.3 states this loss of significance. The abstract's broader all-category statement is not adopted.

all_questions.question: What did the continuous adjusted analyses report?
all_questions.answer: Per 1 mg/kg/min higher eGDR, Model 3 reports OR 0.83 (95% CI 0.81–0.85) for hyperuricemia and OR 0.83 (0.79–0.87) for gout. These are prevalence-odds associations.

all_questions.question: Does this demonstrate that raising eGDR will prevent disease?
all_questions.answer: No. The cross-sectional design cannot establish temporal order or a preventive intervention effect. Gout is self-reported and eGDR is a calculated proxy.

all_questions.question: What design, sample and mortality follow-up were used?
all_questions.answer: The NHANES 2007–2018 analytic sample included 5,837 participants and 906 deaths, with a mean follow-up of 6.5 years and survey-weighted Cox analysis. Raw participant counts and survey-weighted percentages are different quantities and must not be directly substituted for one another.

all_questions.question: How was short sleep associated with mortality?
all_questions.answer: In fully adjusted Model 3, short sleep (<7 h versus 7–9 h) was associated with all-cause mortality at HR 1.25 (95% CI 1.04–1.51). This is an observational association, not a randomized intervention that shortens or extends sleep.

all_questions.question: How was long sleep associated with mortality?
all_questions.answer: In Model 3, long sleep (>9 h versus 7–9 h) was associated with all-cause mortality at HR 1.50 (95% CI 1.10–2.04). The relative hazard is not an absolute-risk estimate or an individual prognosis.

all_questions.question: What did the sleep-trouble analysis show?
all_questions.answer: Self-reported sleep trouble did not show a statistically significant association with mortality in Model 3: HR 1.04 (95% CI 0.87–1.25), P=0.651. This result for one self-reported indicator does not prove that all sleep disorders have no effect on mortality.

all_questions.question: Should 7.23 hours be interpreted as a prescribed individual target?
all_questions.answer: Restricted cubic splines showed nonlinearity (P<0.001), with an estimated sleep-duration turning point of 7.23 h. The turning point is a model estimate from this dataset, not an intervention-validated sleep prescription or a precise target for every individual.

all_questions.question: What literature did this bibliometric study analyze?
all_questions.answer: It analyzed 17,293 English-language documents after deduplication from a title-based Web of Science Core Collection search covering publications from 1 March 2014 to 1 March 2024. The reported database access date was 25 December 2024; this differs from the publication eligibility cutoff.

all_questions.question: How were the retrieved documents distributed across cancer-management topics?
all_questions.answer: The article reports 1,655 prevention, 2,300 screening, 2,874 diagnosis, 10,298 treatment and 166 rehabilitation documents. These are literature counts in the retrieved corpus, not patients or clinical outcomes.

all_questions.question: Which treatment-related keyword frequencies are directly reported?
all_questions.answer: Table 9 reports targeted therapy 1,069, tumor microenvironment 927, immunotherapy 900 and artificial intelligence 797. These frequencies describe bibliographic attention and should not be interpreted as measures of clinical effectiveness.

all_questions.question: Can this study establish which cancer treatment works best?
all_questions.answer: No. Its original evidence consists of document counts and bibliometric patterns. It does not compare patient interventions or estimate treatment effects; clinical claims discussed from other publications require those primary studies.

all_questions.question: How many participants were studied?
all_questions.answer: The article reports 18 AAA patients and 9 controls: 10/5 in-house and 8/4 external. These numbers describe the two reported cohorts, not additional participants per assay.

all_questions.question: Was this unbiased plasma proteomics?
all_questions.answer: No. The study examined an isolated circulating vesicle-associated fraction with a targeted 92-protein Olink panel. Specimen wording also differs between source sections.

all_questions.question: Which proteins were prioritized?
all_questions.answer: IL-4, IL-6, MCP-1, Neurturin and Oncostatin-M. They are candidate biomarkers in the analyzed samples, not approved diagnostic markers.

all_questions.question: Did all five proteins replicate consistently in external assays?
all_questions.answer: No. Western blot and ELISA differed for MCP-1 direction and Neurturin significance/direction. The evidence should be cited as assay-dependent external evaluation, not uniformly concordant validation.

all_questions.question: What ROC performance was reported?
all_questions.answer: In the article-listed order IL-4, IL-6, MCP-1, Neurturin and Oncostatin-M, AUCs were 0.760, 0.840, 0.800, 0.840 and 0.900. The external group was small and confidence intervals were wide. These are single-marker comparisons, not a combined five-protein model.

all_questions.question: Does the study prove that these proteins predict rupture or are treatment targets?
all_questions.answer: No. It reports association, small external assay/ROC comparisons and computational annotations, not prospective rupture prediction or therapeutic target validation.

all_questions.question: How was the HCCcrds gene framework derived?
all_questions.answer: Single-cell modules supplied the HCCcrds gene set. Analyzed cells: 11,383; Genes from modules M2/M4/M5: 562. Cells and candidate genes are not patient counts or demonstrated causal regulators.

all_questions.question: What role did the circadian reference datasets play?
all_questions.answer: The score was evaluated in separate clock, feeding and sleep-reference data. Reference datasets: GSE10045; GSE150381; GSE39445. Reference-experiment evaluation does not mean HCC patients underwent longitudinal physiological circadian measurements.

all_questions.question: Which HCC subtypes were associated with clinical outcomes?
all_questions.answer: TCGA-LIHC analysis identified CS-H, CS-L and CS-M, with poorer outcomes associated with CS-H. TCGA-LIHC n: 369; Subtypes: CS-H; CS-L; CS-M. Association does not establish that circadian disruption causes liver cancer or constitute a validated clinical decision rule.

all_questions.question: Were external classification and survival analyses performed in identical cohorts?
all_questions.answer: External subtype and survival analyses used overlapping but different cohort sets. Fig. 5A datasets: ICGC_LIRI; GSE14520; GSE54236; GSE104580; Fig. 5B datasets: ICGC_LIRI; GSE14520; GSE54236; GSE27150. Do not claim that all five cohorts validated survival, or add the two four-cohort analyses as eight independent cohorts.

all_questions.question: Do the immune analyses demonstrate immunotherapy benefit?
all_questions.answer: Subtypes differed in proliferation/metabolic programs and inferred immune characteristics. Analyses: Expression enrichment; CIBERSORT; IPS. IPS and immune deconvolution are not an observed immunotherapy-response trial.

all_questions.question: What evidence supports the nominated molecular markers?
all_questions.answer: NNMT and MARCKSL1 were among subtype-associated candidate genes. Evidence: Expression correlation and network prioritization. This evidence synthesis does not claim independent causal intervention or therapeutic validation of these genes.

all_questions.question: What single-cell evidence was analyzed?
all_questions.answer: Four aneurysmal aortic samples yielded 7,343 post-QC cells, 16 populations and nine main cell types. The T-cell analysis included 3,841 cells and eight phenotypes.

all_questions.question: What does pseudotime establish and not establish?
all_questions.answer: Monocle inferred a bifurcated trajectory with two terminal fates and three infiltration states. It reconstructs transcriptional relationships and does not directly observe individual cells changing fate over time.

all_questions.question: How was TIRS derived?
all_questions.answer: The analysis used 968 cell-state DE genes, 437 BEAM fate leader genes and 375 trajectory-ordering genes, with a 374-gene intersection and a final bulk-overlapping TIRS of 50 genes.

all_questions.question: Which candidate biomarkers were selected?
all_questions.answer: The LASSO and SVM-RFE intersection selected FOSB, JUNB, CST7 and TBC1D4.

all_questions.question: How did they perform across public cohorts?
all_questions.answer: In FOSB/JUNB/CST7/TBC1D4 order, AUCs were 0.911/0.917/0.926/0.955 in Dataset 1, 0.982/0.911/0.893/0.857 in Dataset 2 and 0.956/0.887/0.506/0.514 in Dataset 3. Discrimination varied by marker and dataset.

all_questions.question: Were they evaluated in independent human samples?
all_questions.answer: Yes: aortic wall from 5 AAA and 4 controls, and peripheral blood from 24 AAA and 15 controls. Aortic-wall AUCs were 1.000/1.000/0.600/0.800 and blood AUCs were 0.989/0.906/0.933/0.736 in FOSB/JUNB/CST7/TBC1D4 order. The aortic-wall sample was small.

all_questions.question: Does this study establish a clinical diagnostic test or therapy?
all_questions.answer: No. The reported associations, marker discrimination, small human-sample evaluation and supportive mouse expression do not establish prospective diagnostic utility, approved standalone tests or human treatment efficacy.

all_questions.question: Which cohorts contribute the reported LUAD input count?
all_questions.answer: The counts are TCGA-LUAD 497, GSE72094 442, GSE68465 462, GSE50081 127, GSE42127 133, GSE41271 183 and GSE31210 246. Their arithmetic sum is 2090, without participant-level deduplication. The separate 79 immunotherapy records are not added.

all_questions.question: How were the subtypes developed and assessed across cohorts?
all_questions.answer: NMF selected three TCGA clusters from the reported 2091 CRD-related gene entries. NTP assessed template assignment in the six named GEO cohorts with confidence filtering. Results say five cohorts while listing six; this remains retrospective expression assessment.

all_questions.question: What survival pattern was reported for C1, C2 and C3?
all_questions.answer: C2 generally had more favorable survival and C1 generally less favorable survival. Cohort-specific plots do not establish identical ranking everywhere. The TCGA log-rank P of 0.0062 is an association result, not a treatment effect or validated decision rule.

all_questions.question: Do circadian-related expression differences directly measure a patient clock?
all_questions.answer: No direct circadian-phase, sleep or metabolic-flux measurement is reported. Enrichment associates C1 with proliferation, C2 with lipid-metabolic and circadian sleep-wake gene sets, and C3 with immune programs; it does not establish circadian causation.

all_questions.question: What genomic features were associated with the clusters?
all_questions.answer: TCGA annotation analyses associated C1 with greater mutation and copy-number-alteration burdens. These comparisons and inferred stemness scores do not show that clock disruption caused TP53 changes, genomic instability or immune escape.

all_questions.question: Why can C3 show high infiltration and a suppressive immune profile?
all_questions.answer: Expression-based analyses report higher infiltration together with lower IPS, higher S-score and higher inferred heterogeneity for C3. Cell abundance and function are different questions; bulk scores do not directly prove suppressive cellular mechanisms.

all_questions.question: Did the study establish immunotherapy benefit for C3 patients?
all_questions.answer: Checkpoint expression, TIS and SubMap similarity support a response hypothesis. The separately reported 79 reference records are incompletely resolved by cohort and diagnosis, and no prospective subtype-guided response or benefit evaluation is reported.

all_questions.question: What can be concluded from predicted drug-sensitivity differences?
all_questions.answer: Computed displays suggest subtype-associated drug-response metrics. Their axes label estimated AUC while text says IC50, and steroid naming differs between text and supplement. They do not justify clinical chemotherapy or corticosteroid recommendations.

all_questions.question: How should the 151-signature C-index comparison be interpreted?
all_questions.answer: The article reports TCGA-internal C-index values 0.741 for C1 and 0.698 for C2 under Chen EG (2017), and 0.796 for C3 under Ma B (2020). These are retrospective candidate-selection results, with unresolved exact Chen-model attribution and no established external performance or clinical utility.

all_questions.question: Is this a patient study?
all_questions.answer: No. It uses cardiac organoids differentiated from commercial human induced pluripotent stem cells. Human cell origin does not make this a clinical validation, and the source does not provide a verified independent donor count. Source location: Journal Pre-proof PDF pp. 6-7, Methods 2.2-2.3.

all_questions.question: Which source version supports this evidence page?
all_questions.answer: The reviewed file is the 37-page Journal Pre-proof obtained through the author-authorized ResearchGate file channel. The DOI, title and 14-author order match the formal indexed record. The definitive full text has not been compared, and the two cited supplementary files have not been inspected. Source location: Journal Pre-proof cover p. 1 and title page p. 2; Crossref DOI record checked 2026-10-27; PubMed PMID 39984109.

all_questions.question: What do the n=3 and n=6 labels mean?
all_questions.answer: They are the sample labels reported in individual figure legends. The paper does not clearly distinguish independent donors, differentiation batches and technical repeats, so the labels are retained without assigning a synthetic total n or claiming independent patient replication. Source location: Journal Pre-proof PDF p. 12, Methods 2.14; legends on PDF pp. 16, 18, 20, 22 and 25.

all_questions.question: What glucose and lipid conditions were examined?
all_questions.answer: The viability screen used a 48-hour exposure, with palmitate conditions from 50 to 300 micromolar and displayed glucose conditions from 5 to 50 mM. The combined-condition panels use 200 micromolar palmitate and varying glucose. These are culture conditions, not clinical targets or patient dosing instructions. Source location: Journal Pre-proof PDF p. 8, Methods 2.5-2.6; Figs. 2B-C and 3.

all_questions.question: What is the defensible injury evidence?
all_questions.answer: The accepted evidence includes CCK-8 signal, BAX/APAF1 transcription, TUNEL staining and selected inflammatory/fibrosis-associated readouts in labeled organoid groups. No exact effect sizes are reconstructed from bars, and these assays do not demonstrate a complete causal mechanism in patients. Source location: Journal Pre-proof PDF pp. 15-22, Figs. 2B-C, 3B-C, 4 and 5; Results 3.3-3.5.

all_questions.question: Does the metformin experiment establish a treatment regimen?
all_questions.answer: No. Three labeled groups are compared and selected readouts shift toward control values after metformin, but the acquired file does not state the metformin concentration. The observations cannot establish a reproducible dose-response regimen, safety or human efficacy. Source location: Journal Pre-proof PDF pp. 11, 23-25, Methods 2.12, Results 3.7 and Figs. 7-8.

all_questions.question: Why are some transcript and mitochondrial conclusions excluded?
all_questions.answer: The broad TNNT2/MYH6 prose descriptions differ from the directions shown in the plots. Methods 2.11 states a red/green JC-1 ratio while Fig. 6B labels green/red. Those details are not reconciled by guesswork or promoted as confirmed findings. Source location: Journal Pre-proof PDF pp. 11, 17-18 and 23-24; Methods 2.11, Results 3.4/3.7, Figs. 3D/H, 6B and 7.

all_questions.question: Has the study validated a physiologically mature heart or a clinical screening platform?
all_questions.answer: No. Morphology and lineage-marker staining characterize a construct, but do not establish adult-heart maturity, clinical prediction or performance across independently characterized donors. No prospective patient validation or direct comparative test proving superiority to every 2D or animal model is reported. Source location: Journal Pre-proof PDF pp. 12-16, Results 3.1-3.3 and Figs. 1-2; Discussion pp. 26-30.

all_questions.question: What is PTMLS in this study?
all_questions.answer: PTMLS is an expression-based post-translational modification learning signature, developed in TCGA-LUAD and evaluated across six GEO survival cohorts using algorithm selection that includes validation-set comparisons.

all_questions.question: Was the prognostic model tested outside the discovery cohort?
all_questions.answer: The article applied it to six GEO LUAD datasets. These are retrospective datasets and not evidence that clinical decisions based on the score improve outcomes.

all_questions.question: Which tumor immune phenotype is linked with high B4GALT2 in patient tissue?
all_questions.answer: In a 171-case institutional LUAD tissue series, higher B4GALT2 expression was associated with CD8-low/desert-like patterns and less favorable survival, without causal assignment.

all_questions.question: What does the B4GALT2 knockdown experiment add?
all_questions.answer: It adds culture-based and mouse-tumor perturbation evidence, including increased CD8 effector readouts with anti-PD-1 combination in mice. This does not establish human treatment efficacy.

all_questions.question: Was Figure 2 corrected after publication?
all_questions.answer: Yes. The original differential-gene heatmap was corrected in an official June 2025 notice (DOI 10.1136/jitc-2024-010787corr1). Use the corrected figure for specific PTM-gene claims.

all_questions.question: Is the mouse inoculation cell count unambiguous?
all_questions.answer: No. Methods reports 2×10^5 cells while the Figure 8H caption reports 1×10^6 cells; the evidence summary does not choose between these conflicting numbers.

all_questions.question: What does the Stage II DNB signal establish?
all_questions.answer: Stage II had the highest reported network instability signal. DNB genes: 36. Cross-sectional stage comparisons do not establish longitudinal prediction of each patient's future deterioration time.

all_questions.question: Is TCPSLevel already a clinically validated prospective risk tool?
all_questions.answer: TCPSLevel was associated with clinical and outcome differences. Expression bins: 100; Background samplings: 1,000; Reported survival cutoff: 0.4. The reported cutoff is not a cross-cohort locked clinical threshold. Grouping rules used in other analyses are not automatically equivalent.

all_questions.question: How were the thyroid molecular subtypes evaluated externally?
all_questions.answer: The ensemble analysis yielded three molecular subtypes. Candidate combinations: 20; Selected combination: CV-PAM; Reported external NTP datasets: 6. Methods 2.6 prints GSE333630 whereas other locations use GSE33630. These are not silently rewritten as a fully verified accession inventory.

all_questions.question: Does miniPC classify subtypes or directly prove improved survival?
all_questions.answer: miniPC classified the consensus subtype labels using a compact gene set. Candidate genes: 296; Final genes: 12; Final classifier: Neural network; External classifier cohorts: 5. This is subtype classification, not prospective individual survival-benefit validation. Unverified figure-only accuracy or AUC values are not reconstructed.

all_questions.question: How many independent donors support the single-cell analysis?
all_questions.answer: Single-cell analysis localized expression patterns across cellular compartments. Reported donors: 1; Cells in Methods: 17,709; Cells in Results: 17,518; Annotated populations: 7. A single donor and a large cell count do not establish large-population replication. No explanation for the count difference is invented.

all_questions.question: What human and experimental evidence supports ASPH?
all_questions.answer: ASPH was evaluated in human tissues and through TPC-1 silencing. Tumor specimens: 48; Adjacent specimens: 48; TPC-1 silencing: Reduced proliferation and migration. Paired tissues are not 96 independent patients. ASCL2-ASPH network inference is not direct binding validation, and cell effects do not establish human targeted-treatment efficacy.

all_questions.question: Were CMap-nominated compounds shown to benefit patients?
all_questions.answer: IPS and CMap supplied candidate immune/drug-response hypotheses. Evidence: Computational scoring and signature matching. Predicted compounds are not proven effective treatments. IPS is not an observed outcome in patients receiving immunotherapy.

all_questions.question: Does this reply introduce another patient cohort?
all_questions.answer: No. It discusses previous modeling work and contains no new cohort or clinical outcome analysis.

all_questions.question: What do 12 and 132 count?
all_questions.answer: They count learners and candidate modeling schemes described from earlier work; they are not numbers of patients or independent validation cohorts.

all_questions.question: How is model selection explained?
all_questions.answer: The authors describe averaging concordance across validation techniques as part of a consensus strategy for selecting a scheme.

all_questions.question: Does the SHAP discussion establish unbiased or causal feature effects?
all_questions.answer: No. It explains the chosen attribution method, without a new experiment proving elimination of bias or causal interpretation.

all_questions.question: How many single-cell patients were studied and how many cells were retained?
all_questions.answer: Eight donor tumor specimens were analyzed (four BRCA1-MT, four BRCA1-WT), generating 32,386 quality-controlled cells; cell counts must not be reported as independent participant counts.

all_questions.question: Was there a genotype-matched spatial comparison?
all_questions.answer: Only four BRCA1-WT spatial transcriptomic samples were described. The spatial analysis cannot independently validate BRCA1-MT versus WT spatial differences in a matched specimen design.

all_questions.question: What evidence nominates ISG15?
all_questions.answer: ISG15 was associated with myCAF-related modules, spatial expression and paired proteomic observations. These are multi-modal correlations and do not directly prove its functional mediation.

all_questions.question: How well did the ICI response model discriminate?
all_questions.answer: The selected KNN classifier reported AUC 0.60 (95% CI 0.51–0.69) for validation and 0.61 (95% CI 0.51–0.71) for testing in the external-treatment source data.

all_questions.question: Was the ICI model validated in treated TNBC patients?
all_questions.answer: No. The Discussion explicitly identifies the lack of validation in ICI-treated TNBC cohorts; it is inappropriate to claim established TNBC treatment selection.

all_questions.question: Did the model-selected groups have significantly different TCGA TNBC overall survival?
all_questions.answer: No. The reported TCGA TNBC overall survival comparison was P=0.182, not statistically significant. A nominal METABRIC comparison does not establish ICI clinical benefit.

all_questions.question: How many ICI cohorts did the authors use?
all_questions.answer: The article is inconsistent: Methods describes 13 pretreatment ICI cohorts (829 records) whereas Results mentions 12 cohorts. Four cohorts pooled as 661 records for the principal development split can be identified; the other cohort count is not silently harmonized.

all_questions.question: Which three strategies are proposed?
all_questions.answer: Crew dental capability, remotely guided care with virtual and 3D technologies, and adapted AI-driven robotic treatment are proposed.

all_questions.question: Why does crew training appear alongside specialist staffing?
all_questions.answer: The authors recognize limited onboard personnel and propose strengthening basic dental training when dedicated specialist staffing is impractical.

all_questions.question: What constraints are acknowledged for remote care?
all_questions.answer: The letter identifies signal delay and distortion, and discusses sensing and communications improvements as proposed responses.

all_questions.question: Were AI dental robots tested in astronauts or microgravity?
all_questions.answer: No. The letter discusses an external technology example and proposes adaptation, without reporting such an experiment.

all_questions.question: Is this a human DCM treatment trial?
all_questions.answer: No. It uses DOX-injured cell systems and mouse models. Human iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes remain an in-vitro system, not treated patients.

all_questions.question: What is being delivered: exosomes or liposomes?
all_questions.answer: The experimental carrier is a peptide-functionalized liposome carrying a miR-185-5p inhibitory payload. The exosome-related title and earlier expression work should not be read as a clinical exosome infusion.

all_questions.question: How were the particles characterized?
all_questions.answer: The loaded formulation had a DLS diameter of 172.35 ± 0.8 nm, encapsulation efficiency of 98.0 ± 1.2% and approximately 80% release at 48 hours. TEM describes approximately 100-nm morphology; that is not the same measurement as hydrodynamic size.

all_questions.question: What evidence supports cardiac targeting?
all_questions.answer: The targeting-peptide preparation showed greater cardiac fluorescence than the non-targeted preparation in the reported mouse comparison. Fluorescence does not by itself quantify an intact active-drug dose or establish exclusive heart delivery.

all_questions.question: What cardiac and cellular outcomes were reported?
all_questions.answer: Mouse echocardiography and histology showed favorable changes under the tested conditions, and cell experiments showed changes in apoptosis- and cuproptosis-associated proteins. These are preclinical readouts, not human outcomes.

all_questions.question: Does the article establish safety or a survival benefit in people?
all_questions.answer: No. Its tolerability testing is limited and experimental. Abstract-only survival and percentage claims are not treated here as independently verified key outcomes, and no human treatment cohort is present.

all_questions.question: What model was used to study ICI cardiotoxicity?
all_questions.answer: B16F10-bearing female C57BL/6J mice were studied under anti-PD-1 treatment; the study also included a dual anti-PD-1 plus anti-CTLA-4 experiment. Human GSE180045 data provided supportive associations.

all_questions.question: What cardiac effects were observed after MCC950 in mice?
all_questions.answer: The tested anti-PD-1 mouse experiments reported mitigation of cardiac injury across cTnT, echocardiography, immune infiltration, apoptosis, fibrosis and inflammatory/chemokine readouts.

all_questions.question: What does the human GSE180045 analysis contribute?
all_questions.answer: Public human PBMC single-cell data show supportive NLRP3/IL1B patterns in monocytes/neutrophils associated with ICI use/myocarditis. These are associations, not a human MCC950 intervention or efficacy-validation cohort.

all_questions.question: What did cardiac scRNA-seq show?
all_questions.answer: The analysis described 68,058 cells, 14 clusters and eight immune classes. Anti-PD-1 increased Macrophages1/3, while MCC950 reduced them and increased reparative Macrophages2. Six hearts per sample were pooled; cells are not independent mice.

all_questions.question: What did macrophage depletion contribute mechanistically?
all_questions.answer: Clodronate depletion effects and TNF/CXCL/CCL communication changes supported a macrophage/T-cell inflammatory network in the mouse model, without definitively assigning every effect to one canonical NLRP3 pathway.

all_questions.question: What happened in the dual-ICI mouse experiment?
all_questions.answer: With n=8 per group, MCC950 mitigated cardiac phenotypes during anti-PD-1 plus anti-CTLA-4 treatment and was associated with reduced tumor burden in the tested B16F10 model.

all_questions.question: Does this study establish MCC950 as a human treatment?
all_questions.answer: No. The intervention, tumor and treatment-after-injury findings are preclinical. The latter was a mouse treatment-after-injury experiment with ameliorated echocardiographic impairment, and does not establish human efficacy, safety or approved use.

all_questions.question: What is the human evidence for KIF13B in atherosclerosis?
all_questions.answer: KIF13B was lower in 40 atherosclerotic versus 40 non-atherosclerotic arterial-wall samples in GSE40231 and in advanced versus early carotid lesions (n=6 tissue samples per group). These are tissue associations; no human KIF13B intervention or causal human effect was tested.

all_questions.question: Did Kif13b loss worsen mouse plaques independently of circulating lipids?
all_questions.answer: Global Kif13b deletion in the Ldlr-deficient model worsened plaques and increased total cholesterol and triglycerides, so that comparison is lipid-confounded. Lyz2-Cre myeloid deletion and Kif13b-deficient donor-marrow transfer worsened lesion, necrotic-core, macrophage and apoptotic-cell outcomes without corresponding plasma-lipid changes in their tested mouse models. These approaches are not macrophage-exclusive.

all_questions.question: What do the single-cell experiments show, and how many independent libraries were there?
all_questions.answer: Public datasets and the study-generated aortic comparison implicated macrophage state changes with lower Kif13b. The generated experiment pooled five mice into one library per genotype, not five independent libraries. Its Results describe 20 weeks of Western diet while Figure 3E describes 12 weeks of high-fat diet, so this page does not resolve the duration. Figure 3 uses one GSE155513 library per 8-week and 26-week time point.

all_questions.question: Is MERTK involved in the efferocytosis phenotype, and was it rescued in vivo?
all_questions.answer: Kif13b-deficient BMDMs had lower MERTK protein and impaired efferocytosis. Restoring MERTK in deficient BMDMs improved efferocytosis, supporting functional involvement in cells. This was not a demonstrated in vivo MERTK-restoration therapy or human treatment.

all_questions.question: How certain is the proposed KIF13B–ITCH–CBL–MERTK mechanism?
all_questions.answer: Unchanged Mertk mRNA, faster MERTK protein loss, proteasome-sensitive degradation, increased MERTK ubiquitination, KIF13B–ITCH interaction and ITCH overexpression rescue support a post-translational model. The precise proposed ITCH-mediated CBL ubiquitination/degradation step was not fully demonstrated; alternative routes including CBL self-ubiquitination remain possible.

all_questions.question: What did NX-1607 do in cells and mice, and what safety findings were reported?
all_questions.answer: In BMDMs, NX-1607 at 50 nM increased MERTK and 50–100 nM improved efferocytosis. In mice, 5 mg/kg/day was given only for the final 16 weeks of a 20-week Western-diet protocol, reducing plaque-related outcomes without reported lipid change. ALT/AST showed no reported liver-toxicity signal, but white blood cells and lymphocytes declined. This is preclinical intervention, not reversal after 20 completed weeks of established disease.

all_questions.question: Has NX-1607 shown clinical benefit for atherosclerosis?
all_questions.answer: No human atherosclerosis treatment efficacy was tested. NCT05107674 is a Phase I advanced-malignancy study, not an atherosclerosis trial; its existence does not establish clinical vascular benefit.

all_questions.question: Does NX-1607 prove the endogenous CBL mechanism?
all_questions.answer: No. The article describes NX-1607 as a CBL inhibitor, whereas external authoritative drug-development sources identify it as a CBL-B/CBLB inhibitor. CBL and CBLB are distinct genes. The observed preclinical rescue cannot by itself unambiguously assign the drug effect to the endogenous CBL mechanism proposed in this paper.

all_questions.question: What model did the IPPS study select?
all_questions.answer: A 13-gene Lasso-plus-SuperPC model was selected from 101 candidate combinations. The five GEO evaluation cohorts also contributed to gene screening and algorithm selection.

all_questions.question: What survival performance can be quoted without resolving the GSE31210 discrepancy?
all_questions.answer: The text and Figure 2H agree on TCGA AUCs of 0.80, 0.79 and 0.78 at 1, 3 and 5 years. They describe the development cohort and must not be presented as independent external performance.

all_questions.question: Were the five GEO cohorts untouched independent test sets?
all_questions.answer: No. Results 3.1 uses the six TCGA/GEO cohorts for survival-based gene screening, and Results 3.2 selects the final algorithm using the mean C-index across the five GEO cohorts.

all_questions.question: Does the OAK/POPLAR analysis verify an objective immunotherapy-response classifier?
all_questions.answer: No. The reported contrast uses overall survival greater than 12 months versus less than 6 months, despite CR/PR and PD/SD labels. This does not establish independently verified objective-response prediction or treatment benefit.

all_questions.question: Were the proposed drugs tested as IPPS-guided treatments?
all_questions.answer: The reported analysis uses oncoPredict, pRRophetic, CTRP and PRISM to infer drug sensitivity. It does not demonstrate patient benefit from selecting a drug using IPPS.

all_questions.question: What is AIHFLevel?
